#4340. Tenebris Somnia Review – A Hair-Raising And Entertaining Throwback

Tenebris Somnia channels the old-school appeal of classic point-and-click adventures, survival horror, and full-motion-video (FMV) experiences, then smartly modernizes them to create a creepy, entertaining experience. Surviving the twisted threats of a demonic dream world is a tightly packed adventure that rewards you with what’s essentially an impressive indie horror film peppered throughout. It’s a nightmare you may not want to wake up from.

The blend of live-action and in-game storytelling works well in Tenebris Somina’s adventure, which begins when protagonist Julia visits the apartment of her filmmaker ex-boyfriend, Ivan, after suffering recurring nightmares of him being massacred by monsters. What begins as a well-meaning check-in on his status spirals down an unsettling rabbit hole when Julia’s worst fears are realized and then some. The dialogue-free tale presents a scary but fascinating exploration of obsession, both in art and in romance, that constantly delivers surprising, and at times upsetting, revelations during its eight-hour runtime. While Tenebris Somnia sometimes leans a little too far into “tell, don’t show” territory when explaining the cool lore of its supernatural threats, I never felt lost or confused about the wild things that regularly unfold on screen.

FMV experiences are nothing new, but Tenebris Somnia’s live-action scenes are a highlight. They’re well shot, sport impressively gruesome practical effects, and even present visual clues that make them important to gameplay. These scenes are additive, never taking too much time away from the in-game action, and they feel well placed to elicit the strongest emotional response. I also appreciate how the live scenes fit thematically, as much of Tenebris Somnia’s tale centers on a horror film shot by Ivan and Julia that significantly impacted their former relationship; at times, it’s like watching a movie about the movie. While I enjoy smaller moments, like opening a door to trigger a live-action jump scare, the filmmaking succeeds in selling Julia's emotions and the cast's reactions. Seeing real fear, concern, and determination in Julia’s eyes as she navigates a dreamworld made up of Ivan’s memories helped endear me to what would otherwise be a featureless pixel sprite.

Gameplay may look unimpressive due to its old-school adventure game presentation, but Tenebris Somnia’s spin on familiar survival-horror mechanics hits the right notes. Taking place entirely within a dreamlike version of a four-story apartment building, you’ll traverse floors collecting and combining objects and deciphering clues to solve well-crafted puzzles. I’m impressed by how well the game’s puzzles make the most of its limited graphical presentation, including clever scenarios involving mirror/screen reflections I won’t spoil, and how consistently creative they are. One devious exercise even utilizes the game’s limited save points as an unexpected resource in a way that changes how you approach your adventure going forward. No matter how strange puzzles become, they are never opaque, requiring just enough out-of-the-box thinking to make me feel smart when I connect the dots.

Battling grotesque monsters (which, naturally, look even creepier in live-action) also feels good, with melee and gunplay sporting deliberate animations reminiscent of classic adventure games without feeling mechanically clunky. Taking on multiple enemies by swinging a pipe or blowing them away with a shotgun feels better than it looks, and the most intense encounters end just as they approach the line of becoming overwhelming.

Boss battles, perhaps most unexpectedly for a largely puzzle-focused adventure, are fun and distinct from each other, be it wave-based bouts against small gremlin-like foes, protecting a fragile effigy of yourself from a parade of demented house servants, or battling literal mirror images of a tentacled flesh monster the Resident Evil series would be proud to claim. Managing limited ammo and health strikes a good balance of feeling tense but not oppressive. Playing conservatively is rewarding, as few non-boss threats need to be engaged if you can evade them well enough. But when I did find myself down to my last bullet or on the verge of death, Tenebris Somnia lets you feel the pinch just long enough before dropping a box of bullets or a health vial at the right moment.

Tenebris Somnia mines the enjoyable nostalgia of playing the horror games of yesteryear without feeling dated in the worst way. Weaving a solid indie horror film adds to the experience rather than feeling like a gimmick. The result is a captivating, well-executed survival-horror romp that maintains a hair-raising atmosphere with a fraction of the pixels of other genre giants.

#4339. Rumble Heroes tier list - All playable heroes ranked

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version: 2.2.138

A blend of side-scrolling RPG and idle games set in portrait orientation was probably the last thing anyone expected to be successful. But thanks to the gorgeous pixelated 2D art style, one-hand playability, and tremendous amounts of exploration and game modes, Rumble Heroes has made its mark on mobile. That said, the story is as generic as it gets. Like, seriously, a princess getting kidnapped and needing to be rescued? Mario already did that years ago! Although he keeps doing it, I suppose...

Having up-to-date knowledge regarding the meta heroes and teams in Rumble Heroes is quite crucial if you’re looking to play the game long-term. RUMBLE HEROES TIER LIST: RANKING THE BEST HEROES When it comes to picking the best heroes, the natural answer should be quality over quantity. By that, I mean, the higher their rarity, the stronger they are. Heroes come in four unique rarities – Legendary, Epic, Rare, and Uncommon. Their strength follows in descending order. You can check the rarity of the hero from the colour of their background.

That’s not the end of the story, though. As many veterans of the community have established, some Epic and Rare heroes are also top-tier in their own right. Some even more than their legendary relative. You see, that’s where “hero synergy” plays a part. Each hero brings a set of abilities that can work in multiple team compositions.

We’ve tried our best to gather all the information relating to the best heroes at the moment. You can take advantage of this tier list to find out where your personal favourites lie, or just to have a general idea of which heroes you should aim to get. Hey now, we’ve all had our bad share of gacha luck, but that’s part of the experience. Once you get your hands on the top-tier heroes, all the pain eases out!

Just a heads up, the developers at Play Hard Lab like to tinker around with their heroes a lot in balance updates. So, we would advise you to bookmark this page as we will ensure to keep the tier list updated in regards to the changes.

If you’re going to be in need of a healer, then look no further than the righteous and virtuous Holy Mace Paul. Wielding a hard-hitting, large iron hammer which he proclaims to be blessed by God, Paul isn’t your regular knight. He might give the impression of a barbarian, but he’s not that kind of beast. In fact, Paul is quite knowledgeable and articulate in his combat ways. You can expect to deal a ton of AoE damage to enemies nearby while keeping your allies topped up on health as well. His healing capacity easily matches actual healers, and oh, the damage is just the cherry on top of the cake.

If you want to recruit a cowboy straight out of the wild, wild west, then Double Gun Mary is going to be your best shot! She just loves shooting bullets, sometimes even without bothering to aim much. Her usability as a ranged damage dealer is unparalleled in the early-mid game since she’s blessed with good attack speed and attack damage. Mary’s basic skill allows her to pinpoint her targets and shoot recklessly towards them, dealing a barrage of continuous damage.

Ever thought of going back in time, perhaps to traditional tribal culture? Well, Brave Uva is a proud tribe member! Sadly, his natural instinct to hunt and hurt is still quite active, making him more of a problem than an advantage. Still, violence always has its uses, especially when you have some dirty kidnappers who need to be taught a lesson. Uva’s basic ability allows him to do a small AoE attack that can inflict enemies with the coveted Poison debuff. He’s also able to command some natural powers, being able to summon thorns to damage enemies from afar.

Now, I know that the bottom of the Rumble Heroes tier list holds some of the most detested heroes, but in all honesty, some of them are quite decent and work well in the right team composition. The perfect example of such a use case isIce Bobo, an enigmatic snowboard surfer turned knight. The little guy has a lot of power packed onto his shield and swords, being able to make use of the Frostbite effect. His ability to chain crowd-control enemies is plausible. Plus, his 2nd ability also empowers allies by providing them with a tiny bit more attack.

I am personally not a fan of pirates, but they do look cool! It seems no love has been shown to the pirate captain Big Hammer Joe, though. He’s quite sturdy, that said, capable of reducing incoming damage and dealing AoE targeted damage. While hammers are not known to be a weapon that can deal AoE damage, Joe’s abilities are all AoE-based.

#4338. The Sims developer vows "our values are unchanged," as it teases multiple projects from post-Saudi-owned EA

The team behind one of EA's most diverse franchises has issued a statement about its future under the soon-to-be Saudi-owned publisher.

In their (slightly belated) new years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are currently working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s new ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.)

Some of these projects will see more playtesting throughout 2026, so you should probably sign up for The Sims Labs if you want to hear about when/how you can get involved.

#4337. PHYSINT Star Bill Skarsgård has Become ‘Enamored’ with Hideo Kojima and His Works

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

If a single person could be considered to be the definitive face of auteur game development, it would be Hideo Kojima, hands down. The man was already showing his chops in putting together unforgettable productions back in the Metal Gear Solid days, and ever since going into business for himself with Kojima Productions, his worlds and stories have only gotten bigger and bolder.

All of those qualities alone more than qualify Kojima for auteur status, but there’s also a little bit more to it than that. Kojima possesses, for lack of a better term, a certain magnetism, both in his person and his production, that inexplicably draws powerful, prominent individuals from across the entertainment spectrum. You just have to look at the original Death Stranding and its star-studded cast to see the kind of magnetic pull a Kojima trip possesses.

Very little is currently known about PHYSINT, one of Kojima’s next big-budget productions that was rescued from the brink by XBOX when Sony bailed out over the summer, but apparently, its star, Bill Skarsgård, was already well aboard Mister Kojima’s wild ride well before he signed on. He spoke to this during a recent appearance on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, as well as the inherent power that comes with Kojima’s works.

Joining an already stacked cast for PHYSINT, which features Charlee Fraser, Don Lee, and Minami Hamabe, is none other than Bill Skarsgård.

As Skarsgård explained, he grew up playing Kojima’s games during his time at Konami, chief among them the Metal Gear series. By his own admission, Skarsgård has played every single Metal Gear game that is commercially available, finding himself repeatedly drawn into the elaborate, intricate world that Kojima was piecing together story-by-story.

Skarsgård has played every single Metal Gear game that is commercially available.

As Skarsgård became more interested in Kojima’s creations, he became more interested in Kojima himself. “I was very enamoured by him and the sort of the mythology or the universes that he creates, but also the sort of mystique and allure about him as well,” he explained.

Hideo Kojima shared several new details about PHYSINT, and it looks like the legendary developer is going back to full stealth.

Later in the interview, as Skarsgård described the process of motion capture that was going into PHYSINT’s development, he marveled at how the planned game will feature both eight hours of narrative alongside an entire, living world populated by photorealistic people and settings.

“I think he's a pioneer, and keeps going out to untrodden waters,” he said of Kojima.

Skarsgård briefly recalled a discussion he had about filmmaking with Kojima during PHYSINT’s motion capture process. It’s no secret that, in addition to video games, Kojima is well-versed in the cinematic arts, both on a technical level and just as a good old fashioned lover of movies, as you can tell from the many film references and direct shout-outs that pepper his games.

Interestingly, though, when Skarsgård asked Kojima if he ever wanted to make an actual movie someday rather than a game, Kojima said no, because he wants to make something with the cinematic potential of traditional film combined with the inherent interactivity of a video game, and a regular film can’t do that. “At this point, what he's doing is inventing a new medium,” Skarsgård said.

All we currently know about PHYSINT, aside from its major stars in Bill Skarsgård, Charlee Fraser, Ma Dong-seok, and Minami Hamabe, is that it’s apparently going to be an action-espionage game in a similar vein to the Metal Gear series. The promotional tagline on its initial reveal poster is “The Next Cold War Begins.” Based on Skarsgård’s gushing, though, it’s going to be quite the ambitious multimedia project, the kind of elaborate, once-per-generation creation that only an auteur like Kojima could bring to life. So, y’know, business as usual.

New PHYSINT exhibition displays feature Metal Gear-like mechs, offering an intriguing glimpse of Kojima's next spy-action game.

#4335. Saint Seiya Awakening tier list of the finest knights in the game

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version: 1.6.58 - Latest Additions: Aries Gateguard We’ve ranked each Knight in the game in separate tiers, taking into account a few important factors, such as base rarity, active and passive abilities, and their Auras. Additionally, we’ve also considered the community rankings presented by veterans of the game that reflect the current meta. So, rest assured, you will find your favourite Knight ranked on our Saint Seiya Awakening tier list! Looking for similar turn-based RPGs? Take a look at our FFVII Ever Crisis tier list that ranks all of your favourite characters, and our Tower of God tier list, along with a reroll guide. Having a clear and conscious understanding of all the Knights and their place in the meta is going to be very beneficial for any player. Based on the popular light novel/manga series by Masami Kurumada, Saint Seiya Awakening is a beautiful mobile JRPG featuring strategic turn-based combat. Stunning animations, lucid particle effects, and anime-stylised full HD graphics are just some of the cherries to pick through when praising it. I have personally observed the benefits you can enjoy once you make use of the strongest Knights, be it for PvE or PvP game modes. PICK THE BEST KNIGHTS I have compiled a complete list of all the currently available Knights, placing the strongest in S Tier and the weakest in E Tier. Of course, tier lists are always subjective in nature, but I would suggest you add the S-tier Knights to your rosters right away if you can, to enhance their overall strength.

Keep an eye out for future changes to our Saint Seiya Awakening tier list, particularly after a balance patch or feature-rich update where new Knights are released. The rankings of individual Knights will be revised based on the balance changes. With that said, simply click on the big blue button below to view the complete tier list!

Poseidon Seraphina is a powerful Support Saint equipped with cost-effective single-target control mechanics. As the battle progresses, she supplies a variety of buffs to herself and her allies, hence strengthening the lineup in the late game.

Goddess Sasha is a Support Saint with the ability to boost attributes as well as defence, counterattacks, and battle assistance. She can also revive herself or her allies with cheat death. Pairing her up with Saints who specialise in basic attacks or damage dealers with low survivability will yield surprising results.

Owl Partita is a Saint specialising in damage reflection. She acquires Reflect DMG through her skills to deal damage to the enemies. One of her skills, Fated Duel, can reduce the damage she takes, allowing her to survive longer as well as trigger Guardian Owl and Eyes of Owl. Both of these abilities help her mark her target and deal extra bonus damage to it.

Goddess Athena is a Saint who deals damage via managing her energy. She gains energy to replenish her reserve and reduces her skill costs when allies spend energy. She shines when paired with allies that have costly skills.

Cain is a great Support saint. His ability, Another Dimension, can significantly disrupt the enemy’s attack. Try to boost his defence attributes and HIT Status to maximise his advantages. His ability, Kishikaisei, can also help revive fallen allies, provided certain conditions are met. However, he does have a few negative quirks, and that puts him in the middle of this Saint Seiya Awakening tier list.

Divine Cloth Hyoga has very powerful single-target damage and control effects. When there are other Ice Saints in play, his skill, Ultimate Diamond Dust, will deal additional damage. Additionally, his Ultimate Freezing Coffin ability freezes an enemy for 1 round and adds 2 stacks of Frostbite. It restores the target's HP and grants Invincibility for 1 round if used on an ally.

Divine Cloth Sagittarius Aiolos is a unique Saint who excels at dealing physical damage and supporting Physical Attack Saints. Under the circumstance in which he consistently provides extra moves, immunity, and damage bonus to said allies, Aiolos is able to swiftly eradicate enemies with Arrow of Justice fuelled by high Arrow Power.

Pandora is a healing-type Saint with very powerful heals. When friendly units have their debuffs removed, her passive is capable of healing large amounts of HP. She also has active heals when needed. Pandora is also great at supporting, and she can transform debuffs into buffs which greatly increases her teammate’s abilities.

Virgo Asmita is a Support Saint who can restrict all the enemies with the Treasures of Heavens, collect Sapindus fruits to create Acala Shields, and purify debuffs on his allies. He is capable of handling all sorts of situations, essentially.

Andromeda Shun has Thunder Wave, a very powerful single-target control skill. He does not have a very high speed, forcing users to reserve energy in order for him to use this skill. Further, enemies afflicted with Thunder Wave cannot be purified.

All of the Knights included at the bottom of the Saint Seiya Awakening tier list are quite bad in contrast to others, as they display no real combat prowess. They are of the lowest rarity, possessing very low base stats in the Attack, Defence, and HP departments. On top of that, a majority of these Knights are power creeped. We highly recommend not investing any of your precious resources into these Knights.

#4334. The Sims 4 gets a bunch of free items inspired by Coach that you can use right now

As part of a free update, The Sims 4 has kicked off a new collaboration with Coach, which means there's free stuff for everyone.

The Sims 4’s first update of the year is here, though it may not be quite what you might have expected. The game’s latest patch mainly centres around a collaboration with Coach, the luxury fashion brand.

This obviously isn’t the game’s first collaboration with a known brand, though this one does include a lot of free items and accessories that anyone can make use of, even if they don’t care about Coach.

The Coach Collection brings nine new items to The Sims 4. They range from clothes and accessories you can use with Create a Sim, to decoration items available in Build Buy. There’s also The Carriage House, a new Gallery household where you can find three new roommates.

There’s a nice bit of variety in the options available, some casual and others more practical for your Sims to wear. Then there’s The Bag Room, which can also be grabbed from the Gallery. The room simply serves as a way for you to show off your Coach bags and trunks collection.

In case you missed it, The Sims’ development team recently shared an update on some of what we can expect in 2026, both for The Sims 4 as well as other projects currently in the works. It even included further confirmation, if any was needed, that Project Rene is a dedicated mobile off-shoot, and not — as many had long believed — The Sims 5.

The blog post also included a statement about EA’s imminent change of ownership, which many fear could alter the series’ inclusive and diverse nature, and the decisions made by its various teams.

#4333. Battlefield 6 Season 2 delayed like many of us expected, but we're getting a new update and a bonus battle pass path

Battlefield 6 has pushed back its next season by nearly a month in order to refine Season 2 content and implement more of players' feedback.

Battlefield Studios has released its first official communication in 2026. Rather than unveil the second season of Battlefield 6, however, the developer instead announced a delay. The currently ongoing Season 1 was initially meant to end on Tuesday, January 20, hence why the developer had to communicate something this week.

Season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off. Given the current sentiment around the game, this news isn’t surprising in the least.

In the blog post announcing the delay, BF Studios said that the decision to extend the current season and push back the start of the next one allows for extra time to “further polish and refine” Season 2 content.

The developer did not offer any hints about Season 2, but there’s an incredibly brief teaser trailer featuring a soldier wearing a gas mask emerging from an environment drenched in toxic gas.

Given that Battlefield 6’s battle royale mode Redsec does not utilise the popular encroaching gas mechanic (using an encroaching ring of fire instead), it’s possible that we may be looking at something new in multiplayer akin to Battlefield 1. Of course, this may just be a visual piece that doesn’t reflect the gameplay of Season 2.

Escalating the fight with new threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj

What we are getting news of today, however, is the game’s next patch. This extension update is going to arrive next week, on January 20, when Season 1 was supposed to end. It’s bringing new weekly challenges to the game, but its biggest addition is yet another Bonus Path to the battle pass. You can also expect the free daily login rewards to continue, alongside other periods of double XP.

Similar to other Bonus Paths, the new Frostfire Bonus Path can be completed alongside the Season 1 battle pass. You’ll need 110 Bonus Path Points in total if you want to earn everything it has to offer, with each tier requiring 10 points. It is worth noting, however, that Frostfire Points are only earned through weekly challenges, meaning there won’t be any bonus challenges associated with it.

Frostfire includes several new customisation rewards, of course, such as a Weapon Package, soldier skin, XP boosts and the usual run of unlocks.

Though the latest blog post may be devoid of any real details on Season 2, BF Studios confirmed that Battlefield Labs will play a larger role in offering a preview of what’s to come, so it’s entirely possible that the testing initiative will soon open its doors to players with an early look at some of the maps and other content planned for Season 2.

#4331. A Mass Effect 5 Trailer Featuring Liara Appears To Have Leaked Following BioWare's Closure

In case you missed the tragic news yesterday, EA laid off 400 employees this week, including all of BioWare. The studio behind Mass Effect, Dragon Age, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and more, has been shut down, and its last remaining project was canceled. The game in question was a fifth entry in the Mass Effect universe, and BioWare shared very little about it – not even an official name. Following the studio's closure, however, a trailer for the sci-fi sequel started circulating around the internet.

While no official BioWare representatives have confirmed that the footage is real, Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier claims that it is. Schreier has a history of credible reporting in the field, and was the first to break the news about the layoffs. IGN has also stated that it confirmed the trailer's legitimacy.

If you want to see for yourself, you can watch the trailer on Reddit.

"The following is in-engine footage form our small team," text at the start of the video reads. "It uses our pre-production assets." The footage shows no gameplay, but includes a good-looking CG cutscene of a new protagonist speaking with an asari woman in a crowded bar. As he tells her about his life, we see glimpses of him as a soldier, then as some kind of spy, traveling to several planets to track down conflicts and "stopping them before they start." After the asari woman reveals that she's been "starting the fires" he's trying to prevent, another woman behind her lowers a hood. This new woman reveals herself as Liara T'Soni, one of Mass Effect's most iconic characters.

Then, Liara and the protagonist team up to take out the woman at the bar and her henchmen, using guns and telekinetic abilities. The trailer fades to black, then fades back in to reveal the game's would-be title: Mass Effect Universe. It's a great-looking trailer – it's a shame the game will never see the light of day.

If you want to join us in grieving BioWare, we republished an oral history of the studio that was originally written by former editor Matt Bertz in 2016. You can also read our cover stories on BioWare's most recent releases: Dragon Age: The Veilguard, Mass Effect: Legendary Edition, Anthem, and Mass Effect Andromeda.

#4330. Girl Wars tier list & reroll guide

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version 1.0.17 - Latest Additions: The Trapped Actress - Nero, Flame Emperor's Heir- Liu Bang, Sorceress of Avalon - Morgan, Achilles- Conquered Valkyrie, Huang Zhong- Chocolate Kitchen Maid, Demon-Eyed Juggernaut - Yagyu Jubei, Invincible Sword- Tsukahara Bokuden, Serve the Mistress - Gilgamesh, Special Private Training Session- Lv Bu, Fairy Queen - Oberon, Blitz Emperor - Caesar

If you are a new player and you want to get a glimpse of the meta game, our Girl Wars tier list will do just that. Find out who the best girls to include in your team are, which ones you shouldn't really bother with, and how to reroll to get the most favourable start.  Girl Wars Tier List: How do we rank the girls? The game has been available in Asia for quite some time now, so we do have a good amount of data available. That said, the girls don't have exactly the same stats, so their ranking evaluation is going to be different.

Currently, there are not many UR girls available, but you should expect this to change soon, as many will be released in the future. And, with future releases, our Girl Wars tier list will obviously change accordingly.

About Tomoe Gozen Tomoe Gozen, with her special abilities, such as damage immunity, powerful counterattacks, and a game-changing ultimate, is an extremely effective girl in PvP (but not just there). She is a well-rounded character who excels in both stats and mechanics. You'll notice that she's a staple in many teams. About Christian Christian is a top-tier support character in Girl Wars, as she excels at controlling her opponents and countering fast-paced playstyles. She has the ability to freeze enemies, which makes her a staple force in PVP.

Here's the thing with SSR girls in Girl Wars. For the most part, they've been outdated by the UR ones. That's power creep for you. In many cases, it's better to use SR girls, especially if you are an F2P player, but more about that on the next page.

Even though it's inefficient to max out SSR girls early on because you don't have many food resources, some of them are still very good and worth the investment. About Siegfried The good thing about Siegfried is that you can get her fragments quite easily. So, for F2P players, she's a good, solid option. Her skill, Spear Thrust, is a powerful attack that deals high damage, drains the target's energy and defence, and boosts block rate. It also has a chance to restore a protective Dragon Blood Mark that makes her immune to normal and skill attacks. About Joan of Arc Arguably the best SSR, Joan of Arc, has both abilities, which are attacks that damage a row of enemies, prioritising those with the Imprisonment status. If the front row target has Imprisonment, it spreads it to the back row enemies. Imprisonment prevents the target from moving and reduces healing.

Some of the best SSRs are Frederick, Diao Chan, Guan Yu (She's a great option as a leader), and Oda Nobunaga.

About Satutobi Sasuke Satutobi Sasuke is a valuable support who can be effective once you upgrade her to seven stars. She provides a 10% attack boost to the entire team and her ultimate significantly increases the critical hit rate and damage for her team.

It is recommended to place her in either position 1 or 3 while using Nene as a substitute in one of these positions for additional synergy. Make sure Sasuke's equipment is the best you can get for her. About Nene Even though I wouldn't suggest investing much in Nene, getting her for free to 7 stars is worth it. Especially if you are F2P, she's going to be helpful in the earlier stages of the game, thanks to her ability that increases the back row damage and the team's attack. Her ultimate decreases enemies' defence. So all in all, she's a very solid support that can fit into pretty much any team. About Honda Komatsu Honda Komatsu is a hybrid healer/damage dealer who attacks enemies with low HP and restores HP to allies. Her skills deal damage, heal, and provide buffs like increased block chance.

#4329. GTA 6 Could Get PC Release Soon to Avoid AI Clones, Says Former Rockstar Dev

Lauren has experience in the gaming and esports space, writing news, guides, features, reviews, lists, conducting interviews, and more. Before joining the team at DualShockers, Lauren was a Features Writer at Adventure Gamers, a Guides Writer at Gameranx, as well as contributing as a News Writer at PCInvasion and Daily

The launch of GTA 6 is imminent, and thanks to Rockstar Games moving the pre-load date forward, the release of this highly anticipated game is starting to feel more real. However, not even the big dogs are safe from the likes of AI, as there are concerns Generative AI could be used by third parties to port the game on PC.

It’s becoming increasingly common to see an indie hit take off and AI-generated clones quickly following in an attempt to piggy back off of that success. One such example is the viral Needle In A Haystack game, which follows the premise of finding a needle hidden in over 10 million pieces of hay with your friends. Since then, various AI-generated rip offs began appearing on Steam, with one developer even stealing the original game’s code.

Rockstar's 38 new GTA 6 screenshots showcase incredibly detailed faces, Vice City's nightlife, and the gangs and scenes bringing Leonida to life.

Roblox is another platform that Needle In A Haystack, among other trending games, has popped up on. Since Roblox is free to play, anyone can play a near copy of a paid game, with a few microtransactions thrown in.

Although GTA 6 would be difficult to replicate in the same way, former Rockstar North technical director, Obbe Vermeij, believes AI is a threat to an official GTA 6 PC port, as discussed in an interview with Rock Paper Shotgun.

Vermeij acknowledges that Generative AI “really has changed the world," and believes, “I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be as good as their effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together. Obviously, I don't really know what they're thinking."

"I don't really see how you could protect against that, to be honest, I don't see it," he says, but Take-Two Interactive aren’t completely powerless on the matter. “But a big company like Take-Two, they would be able to get the lawyers on the case, and maybe, like, you said, for a big game, maybe the AI doesn't really do a particularly good job.”

“But yeah, I mean, it's a brave new world. What was the case before, is that there's so much effort in developing the game, that it is not possible to rip it off, and that's completely changed now. So, yeah, we're going to have to see in the next couple of years, how that's going to pan out."

It has been widely reported that GTA 6 will be released on PC during the first quarter of 2027. Neither Rockstar Games nor Take-Two has provided comment on the status of the arrival of GTA 6 on PC.

Not even the big dogs are safe from the likes of AI, as there are concerns Generative AI could be used by third parties to port the game on PC.

If GTA 6 does make its PC debut in the first quarter of 2027, it would land just a few months after its release on PlayStation 5 and XBOX Series X|S platforms. Therefore, it would be a lot quicker than the PC release of GTA 5, which came out in April 2015, nearly two years after its roll out on console in September 2013.

Any AI-generated ports would likely face a DMCA takedown and will undoubtedly be nowhere near as polished or safe to run than the real deal.

As AI continues to advance, it will be interesting to see if it’s able to replicate a game as huge as GTA 6. The game is expected to require up to 212 GB of storage on console and is packed to the brim with approximately 80 hours of story content alone.

From DMA Design to GTA III, GTA V, and RDR2, let's take a look back at how Rockstar Games changed open-world gaming and why GTA 6 has so much to live up to.

#4328. Zelda: Ocarina Of Time's Director Was Chosen For His Ability To "Solve Problems Very Aggressively"

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 gained a new director in HokWai Ng, a developer at Nintendo who started his career with Wii Fit Plus before becoming involved with planning on Tears of the Kingdom for the Switch.

In a new interview with Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi over on Polygon, Aonuma commented on the reason why Ng was chosen to lead the development on Ocarina of Time. He cited Ng's ability to "solve problems very aggressively, very proactively" during his time on Tears of the Kingdom, while his idea for future projects made Aonuma believe that he would be the right fit for a remake.

"He was involved with the planning on Tears of the Kingdom, and he was someone on that project that I saw find and solve problems very aggressively, very proactively. And so I knew that would be a great opportunity to see him do more. I thought it'd be really interesting to use him on this project. In fact, at the end of Tears of the Kingdom, he started to present some ideas for future projects that made me think, "Okay, yeah, you're interested in something like a remake. I think you've got your own ideas here. Perhaps you should work on this as a director." And this has been a really good experience. I think [it was] a good decision."

It's honestly so lovely to see Nintendo continue to work with younger generations of developers and provide them with such opportunities. It's certainly not something we're used to seeing here in the west, that's for sure.

Needless to say, we think HokWai Ng has done a remarkable job on Ocarina of Time, and we're keen to see what else he might do with the Legend of Zelda franchise in the future.

#4326. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Review - Silver Bullet

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 arrives at a crossroads for the series, thanks in large part to the inconsistent quality of recent entries. With a shaky predecessor, Infinity Ward had a lot to repair and conclude, especially with 4 set to bookend the rebooted Modern Warfare series. Fortunately, backed up by a fun campaign, thrilling multiplayer, and loads of new modes and content, Modern Warfare 4 makes up for the past and then some.

Modern Warfare 4 continues after the events of 2023’s Modern Warfare 3, with Captain Price hellbent on stopping Makarov and his higher-ups. The story features shifting perspectives, from a new group of ragtag Korean soldiers to familiar characters like Gaz. The character dynamics harken back to the original trilogy, especially in the boots-on-the-ground missions with the South Korean unit, led by Park (played by Beef actor Young Mazino).

For a series that, at least recently, has been more spectacle than story, giving the stakes the time they deserve is nice. While it moves away from the stealthy and modernized elements, it makes sense for the matters at hand. The majority of Modern Warfare 4’s attempts at wrapping up the overarching plot of the rebooted series works, but it rushes through some character arcs and story beats in uneven fashion. Furthermore, much of the game’s cast, especially Mads Mikkelson’s Archer and Prisca Kim’s Ri Ju-Young, are underutilized, which is a shame since they both deliver great performances.

Despite the shortcomings of the campaign, Call of Duty's bread and butter, multiplayer, still delivers. While it doesn’t have the fluidity of Black Ops’ newer entries, the customization and design of weapons and maps make it worth digging into. From small, intimate shooting galleries with Mumbai and Nautical to wide free-for-alls like Coal and Reactor U92, the range helps maintain excitement, even if it gets repetitive over time.

The variety of multiplayer modes keeps things fresh on the battlefield. Returning modes like standard Team Deathmatch and Kill Confirmed continue that enjoyable competitive flair that made them the stars that they are. However, new modes like Combat Outpost and Hijack fit right into the already great lineup. In particular, Combat Outpost upscales your typical 6v6 player count to 24v24, leading to more action and teamwork. Hanging onto a team’s tank, shooting enemies from afar, and taking back outposts is exhilarating, even if it can all go bad moments later by a well-placed RPG shot.

Even after hours of gameplay, the variety of options to craft your perfect gun is impressive. Figuring out the best scope, ammo, stock, and muzzle, as well as the advantages and disadvantages of them, is a fun way of customizing your playstyle. Gunny, a mechanic that helps optimize your gun for certain styles, can help with decision paralysis, but I rarely used it. Not many FPSs go that far and Modern Warfare 4’s commitment to the feature makes it stand out.

The newest mode, DMZ, impresses out of the gate. After a few flat attempts in the past, this is the definitive Call of Duty extraction shooter, whether you play solo, or in duos or trios. Immediately, you’re thrust into the wide open world of Hajin and left to fend for yourselves with what you have and what you can gather and extract. Fans of Arc Raiders and Marathon should feel right at home as the gameplay borrows from the typical extraction shooter experience. Intense, action-packed moments keep you coming back after every win or loss. And the excellent gunplay and level design elevate it into something worthwhile, no matter how you play.

Despite not encountering many live players during my time in Hajin in DMZ, it still proves challenging, even for seasoned pros. The world is not your friend, and taking risks can come at a high cost. A good team, as well as a thoughtful loadout and traits, are required to survive. The unpredictability of it all keeps you on your toes, making for an exciting addition to the already strong multiplayer suite.

Regardless of the mode, Modern Warfare 4 is one of the best-looking Call of Duty titles to date. New York and Paris are lifelike, and it truly embodies the realistic, modern aesthetic the series has always aimed to achieve. However, I encountered a few technical hiccups, especially in the campaign. Slow framerate plagues some high-octane scenes and texture loading is frequent across the board. These distractions are far from game-breaking, but enough to be noticeable.

While the plot execution is a bit shaky, engaging multiplayer options, including DMZ, aptly demonstrate that Infinity Ward can still deliver compelling military-FPS experiences. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is a strong return to form that serves as a solid sendoff for the rebooted subseries.

#4325. After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

The Sims Medieval had a short but powerful run back in 2011, and now many of its best features are finally coming to the main franchise.

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free update, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

#4324. Amazon’s Mass Effect TV Series Is Reportedly Still In Production Despite BioWare Closure

EA shut down legendary RPG developer BioWare this week, canceling its in-development fifth Mass Effect game as a result. Despite the closure, Amazon Prime’s upcoming Mass Effect streaming series will proceed as planned, according to a report by IGN.

Amazon MGM Studios began developing a Mass Effect series in 2024. At the time, Mass Effect series executive producer Mike Gamble confirmed the show isn't a retelling of the video games, saying, “The show will explore a brand-new story within the universe's timeline, and will be set after the original trilogy. It won't be a retread of Commander Shepard's story – because after all... that's YOUR story, isn’t it?”

With BioWare’s closure, one would think the series would go up in smoke, but sources within Prime Video speaking to IGN confirmed that it remains in development. Furthermore, all of the creatives involved remain so. This includes showrunners Doug Jung (The Cloverfield Paradox, Star Trek Beyond) and Daniel Casey (F9: The Fast Saga, Wardriver), former Marvel Studios head Avi Arad, and Jessica Jones executive producer Karim Zreik. Mike Gamble was also involved, and this report suggests he still is, but it remains to be seen how his position on the project has changed with BioWare’s demise, given he served as a guiding voice from the studio. The Mass Effect series has no release window.

The Mass Effect series joins other video game adaptations Amazon has in the works, which include a third season of Fallout (with Aaron Paul joining the cast), a live-action God of War series starring Dave Bautista, a live-action Tomb Raider series starring Sophie Turner, as well as series based on Life is Strange and Wolfenstein.

For more on Mass Effect, check out our review of the Legendary Edition and our recently republished Oral History of BioWare from 2016.

Ahead of its official release next week, Arknights: Endfield has already surpassed 35 million pre-registrations from players around the world.

Arknights: Endfield developer Gryphline has a good reason to celebrate, as the upcoming free-to-play action RPG has achieved yet another milestone. The developer announced today that Endfield already has over 35 million pre-registrations.

This a major moment for the game, which is poised to be one of 2026’s biggest releases on mobile.

In December, when Gryphline officially revealed the Arknights: Endfield release date, the developer said at the time that the game had surpassed 30 million pre-registrations, meaning over 5 million more have joined in since then.

Arknights: Endfield has pretty much wrapped up closed testing, and we’re in the final stretch ahead of the January 22 launch, when the free-to-play game will go live across PC (where it'll be available via the Epic Games Store, as well as Gryphline's own launcher), PS5, and mobile platforms (iOS, Android).

The developer hosted a livestream to celebrate, where it also debuted two new trailers: the launch trailer (below), as well as another look at gameplay. The gameplay trailer also shows off more of the game’s Talos-2 world, and sets up the mystery at the centre of its narrative.

If you’re going to be playing Endfield on PC, you’ll be happy to know that you can expert a breezy experience with support for 120fps. #4321. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort Review: Everything Switch Sports Should Have Been

Wuhu Island is back, and so is the magic. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort finally recaptures the charm that made me fall for this series years ago.

Say Nintendo Switch Sports Resort three times in a row. Go on, I’ll wait. It’s a tongue twister of a title, and I tripped over it every single time, which is at complete odds with the smoothness the game delivered.

The Nintendo DS didn’t just have great games, it had ideas that stuck around way longer than anyone expected.

I have played every entry in this series. When the Wii turned waving a remote around the living room into a whole new way of playing, I was right there, and I’ve had a soft spot for motion controls ever since. I do enjoy a good sports game, but if I’m honest, it’s mostly Nintendo’s that get me off the sofa. That’s also why I always worry a little whenever a new one is announced, because Nintendo Switch Sports never quite managed to feel like the series I fell in love with.

DualShockers was given a code for this review, and I’ve spent multiple hours on Wuhu Island so far, mostly in single player, on a docked Switch 2. I am nowhere near 100%, and I suspect that could take hundreds of hours depending on how good you are. But the hours I have put in have been more than enough to know this is the game I wanted Switch Sports to be.

The first thing I noticed was how little I was waiting. Load times are much shorter than in Nintendo Switch Sports, menus snap into place, and you can even rearrange the layout of the sports to suit you. Everything feels smoother, less clunky and quicker to get going. After the last entry, that alone felt like a small miracle.

Nintendo games always feel good, and I went in with high expectations of polish. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort met every single one of them. It ran perfectly on my docked Switch 2, and I didn’t run into a single bug or crash in my time playing this. Why can’t every game feel this polished?

My first birdie in Golf and my first strike in Bowling both made me grin like an idiot. It turns out the muscle memory I built up over years of these games is fully transferable, and it all just feels a bit more refined now. Bowling and Golf are still my favourites, Table Tennis gives you lovely control over every return, and Archery is so satisfying that I kept going back for “just one more” target. Tennis now comes with three courts to choose from, which is nice, if hardly a revolution.

Not everything landed quite as well. Boxing was the one I enjoyed least, because the Joy-Con 2 occasionally lost track of me once I mixed in ducks, hooks and jabs. Volleyball, unfortunately, still feels very sluggish, and that carries over into online play, too. It’s my single biggest deduction, and it’s a shame, because Volleyball also gave me one of my favourite moments.

Picture this: deuce after deuce, a match that seemingly will not end, my arms burning. By the time it was over, I was panting and had to sit down and rethink a few of my life choices. Nintendo, if you’re reading this, I desperately need a new Ring Fit Adventure, because that game actually kept me fit.

Then there’s Thumb Wrestling. It’s such an odd addition, and it makes me laugh every time, because it is so very Nintendo. It’s simple to pick up, there’s more strategy to it than you’d ever expect, and I can already see it causing chaos at parties. And yet.

I cannot believe they included Thumb Wrestling over my beloved Baseball. I’d have taken Disc Golf from the original Wii Sports Resort, too. Some of the racket and net sports also start to blur together after a while, so a little more variety would have gone a long way.

My favourite part of Resort is the trio of Leisure Sports, which have nothing to do with winning and everything to do with simply enjoying the island. Power Cruising puts you on a jet ski, with a Joy-Con held sideways like handlebars, twisting to accelerate and leaning to steer. Prop Plane turns your controller into a little aeroplane in your hand, and Skateboarding uses mouse mode, so you swipe across the table to push off and flick upwards for tricks. Luckily, the Nintendo Switch 2’s Welcome Tour trained me for exactly that moment. Generally, these sports are the most creative controls in the whole game, and they’re where I spent a lot of my down time.

Each of them comes with a Sightseeing Tour, where you have five minutes to explore and collect as much as you can. I’ll admit the timer sometimes had me wishing for more. There is a Free Roam mode without one, but none of the collectibles appear there, so it’s more of a scenic drive than a treasure hunt.

There’s no story in Resort, not really, but the sightseeing is the closest it gets. Finding photo spots and cruising past corners of Wuhu Island I’d never seen before taught me more about the place than any previous entry. It’s also the perfect palate cleanser after a sweaty round of Volleyball.

Hyrule has never looked better as they look in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, and critics seem to agree!

Very quickly I discovered probably the number one reason that will keep me playing for months: everything counts now. In Nintendo Switch Sports, you could only earn the points needed to unlock new outfits and accessories by playing online. In Switch Sports Resort, every game you finish earns you points, single player included, and you spend them in a shop that rotates its collections weekly and monthly. You don’t even need a Nintendo Switch Online Membership anymore!

What you can pull from the shop is random and different for every user. It covers clothes, accessories, name tag options and sporting gear. On top of that, each sport has its own achievements, which you can unlock solo or with friends. As a bit of an achievement collector, that’s dangerous news for my free time.

For anyone who wants more of a challenge, Island Crown sets you up against increasingly skilled CPU players in each sport, with an Island Champ waiting at the top. The first few opponents are almost charmingly bad, but the tougher ones are genuinely tough. Nintendo has also added a little more “canon” this time, with each sport’s champion getting a bit of backstory. I haven’t beaten a single Champ yet, but I’m working on it.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort looks gorgeous. It’s bursting with colour and that typical Nintendo charm, and I never once got tired of looking at it. The soundtrack is upbeat and light-hearted, and returning players will recognise plenty of the sound cues. My favourite detail? In Golf, you can hear the waves crashing against the shore and birds chirping between your shots.

The island itself never feels empty. Miis stroll around in the background, and even the CPU opponents use the little stickers that are the game’s only way of communicating. You can play as the newer-style characters and the classic Miis, which made me happier than I’d like to admit. Every session left me feeling a little brighter, which is exactly what I want from this series.

Accessibility has taken a step forward, too. You can choose your dominant hand for every sport, turn on a colourblind mode, and switch off the emote pop-ups from other players and CPUs if you find them distracting. Golf has assistance options, and the tutorials are clear and helpful. You are still tied to the Joy-Cons and motion controls, though: there are no alternative control schemes, and nothing can be remapped.

This is a game for literally everyone. If you just want some fun, need something to play with your family or friends, or want an excuse to move a bit more, this game has you covered. You can play with one to four people locally, go online, take on CPU opponents, and even team up with a CPU partner in some sports. I can already see it becoming the focal point of many a games night.

What surprised me most is how good it is on your own. It’s the most fun I’ve had in a while, even playing completely alone. Games like this usually lose steam once the novelty wears off, but there’s so much variety here that I’m nowhere near running out of things to do.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort looks gorgeous. It’s bursting with colour and that typical Nintendo charm, and I never once got tired of looking at it.

Online play does have a couple of bumps in typical Nintendo fashion. Bowling has some strange waits between turns, and switching sports kicks you back to the lobby. These are pretty small complaints, though, when everything around them is this good. If anything, Nintendo has undersold this one: for how much better it is than its predecessor, it deserved a much bigger marketing push.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a great revival for a series I’m always a little worried about. Nintendo is one of the only AAA players left that still brings real whimsy to the table, and Resort feels fresh, special, and complete from day one. If you want a sports game with actual substance, rather than a handful of minigames, this is the one. If you’d rather sink into a big story, look elsewhere – and if you hate fun? Honestly, I’m not sure how you ended up reading a review about Wii Sports' cheerful grandchild, but I admire the commitment. Somewhere on Wuhu Island, an Island Champ is waiting for me. I might not be ready yet. But I want to become the Island Legend, so I will keep training.

#4319. Remedy Explains Control Resonant's Most Memorable, Unexpected Sequence And Its [REDACTED] Inspirations

Please allow the first sentence here to warn you that this interview discusses a portion of Control Resonant that takes place near the end of the game and is arguably the most unexpected and surprising sequence. I encourage you to experience it without spoilers. So if you haven't beaten the game yet, please do, and then come back to this page.However, if you have beaten the game, or curiosity has driven you to learn what game has been redacted from the headline and why (it's the 1995 Super Nintendo RPG, EarthBound, by the way), then please read on.

In the late-game of Control Resonant – basically right before you tackle the final confrontation – the game suddenly shifts timeframe and genre to become a 16-bit RPG. The nostalgic lens turns the game into something that feels like 1995's EarthBound, complete with turn-based battles, in order to explain the trauma that Jesse and Dylan went through at a young age after they came across an object of power: the slide projector. The whole sequence is funny, heartbreaking, weird, and importantly effective at making you feel you are seeing a part of their past. It was particularly effective on me as I have fond memories of playing EarthBound and games like it when I was young. To see and experience Dylan and Jesse's childhood this way felt accurate, as absurd as that sounds.

I reached out to Remedy to specifically discuss that portion of the game. You can find the full e-mail interview below with the team members who contributed to its creation.

The big RPG backstory sequence for Jesse and Dylan – why approach the storytelling that way?

Lead level designer, Anne-Marie Grönroos: The basis for the whole sequence is that the Hedron attacks Dylan's mind, breaks his reality apart, and he has to rebuild himself. We wanted the reality-breaking part to affect the game itself and have the player feel some of the confusion Dylan is feeling by breaking the fourth wall.

Who pitched that sequence, how did they pitch it, and was it difficult to sell to the larger team?

Grönroos: At Remedy, ideas rarely come from a single person or team, and we rarely do formal pitches, but rather discuss and workshop ideas cross-craft until they start taking the shape of something we like. The initial idea from the writer was for this to be a text-based adventure, to return to a very early form of a video game to show that the Patterning is devolving him, but an Alan Wake 2 DLC had already done that, and we wanted to find something else.

Independently, some months ago a level designer had suggested a sidequest with JRPG pixel graphics, but that had gone nowhere. I remembered that and suggested doing an old Final Fantasy-style JRPG here, which also felt more fitting since that’s the type of game Dylan and Jesse would have played in their childhood, and not a text-based adventure. People got excited about that, and after some concerns about feasibility, we went forth with it. It helped that the level designer who had originally wanted to do the JRPG side quest is a big fan of these types of games and has made them before. I wouldn’t have dropped something this crazy on someone who wasn’t passionate about it and ready to figure out how to do it with our engine that’s not built for anything like this.

Is EarthBound (Mother in Japan) the primary inspiration for that sequence? Are there big fans of those games at Remedy?

Senior level designer in charge of the JRPG quest, Arhi Makkonen:The whole Quest was born from that childhood feeling I had when playing old JRPGs – Final Fantasy, Breath of Fire, Chrono Trigger, Secret of Mana, Bahamut Lagoon, and yes, Mother. The most important thing for me was capturing that feeling of a time when games felt like magic. I think many people can relate to that nostalgia, and now Jesse and Dylan share that feeling in the game.Visually, Mother was a major inspiration of course. Juuso Anttila is the concept artist who did all the splendid pixel art for Rebuild quest. Mother's style fits the mysterious Americana small town vibe perfectly. We also couldn't pass up the pun about a story revolving around "Not-Mother" that was made in the style of Mother.

Was it difficult to implement the sequence into the game? Did Remedy's Northlight Engine need significant work to account for the sequence?

Makkonen: The Northlight engine was designed to work perfectly for third-person action games. Well, Rebuild Quest is pretty much the opposite of that. Northlight is a specialized tool rather than a general-purpose one, so we had to come up with some rather creative solutions to create a 2D JRPG.

First of all, we’re faking the 2D look. In reality, the entire JRPG Ordinary exists within a 3D world that the camera simply views from directly overhead. It occupies a tiny patch in a remote corner of the game world—a space where 3D Dylan would barely have room to stand. The entire game-within-a-game is written in Lua; our incredibly versatile game designer, Tommi Saalasti, created the underlying system, upon which I was then able to build the story.

Since we didn't really have the tools to create a game like this, I had to hand-code every single detail. Dylan takes one step up, Dylan turns left (where Jesse hopefully is at that moment), text box 1, text box 2. The Lua script for the Rebuild quest alone probably contains as many lines of code as all the other quests in the game combined. And then there were things like animations were restricted to a maximum of two frames, and some UI elements were created using static particle effects.

So yes, we faced all sorts of challenges and compromises, but at the heart of it all was a wonderful story – simply told in a somewhat unconventional way. We trusted that the narrative would make up for some of the imperfections.

Remedy has a reputation for big unexpected and often crazy singular moments. What are the conversations like around delivering those? In pre-production, are there conversations like, "What is the big moment for this one?" Or do they happen pretty naturally?

Grönroos: They both happen naturally and we also have conversations about what the big moments should be. Sometimes we like a section so much that we decide to put even more resources and importance to it, even if it wasn’t supposed to be all that important from the get-go. The Into the Sinkhole quest, for instance, is a quest that wasn’t planned to be a “tentpole moment” from the start, but we kept putting more effort into it when it was shaping up to be something very special.

But most setpieces in the game were planned to be such from the early stages of pre-production. In Resonant, we wanted to have multiple standout moments instead of a single sequence like the Ashtray Maze overshadowing everything else, and I’m happy to see that players have different favorites.

And a different approach from Control is that several of these memorable moments (Sinkhole, Underpass Fault, the JRPG section) are more emotional and subdued instead of bombastic action (although we also have big action setpieces), which was an interesting challenge itself.

Was there a fear that the visuals would limit the emotional impact of the sequence?

Grönroos: Yes, but we decided to trust the writing. Several other games have managed to deliver a similar emotional impact despite pixel graphics (and sometimes because of them, since the level [of] abstraction can make characters more relatable and up to the player’s interpretation), so we weren’t too concerned.

Was there a fear that action game fans would be frustrated by the RPG sequence?

Grönroos: Yes, this was the main concern about the sequence. It was a very polarizing sequence in the playtests: people either loved or hated it. We did discuss shortening it significantly, but in the end decided to keep it as it is but added some fast travel options and make some parts skippable. There were more fans than haters, and we didn’t want to sacrifice something we really enjoyed.

How concerned were you about the actual RPG mechanics of that sequence?

Makkonen: Since Rebuild doesn't feature a vast number of battles, we didn't need to build particularly deep RPG or progression systems. The combat served as an additional storytelling tool – illustrating how bullies torment Dylan, showing his first fight (against rats, naturally), and depicting his eventual abduction by the FBC.

Refining the combat to be simple, yet offer the player meaningful choices required a few iterations. In addition to standard attacks, the children can occasionally use special abilities: Dylan delivers a heavy blow to a single enemy, while Jesse fires at everyone. Enemies deal enough damage that defending becomes necessary when multiple foes target the same character.

The lightbulbs in The Underpass mission goes in similarly unexpected, animated directions. How did that mission come about? What was the pitch like for that one?

Grönroos: That one started with the idea of doing something comically mundane, switching lightbulbs, and adding a paranatural twist to it. The cartoon man wasn’t in the initial version, but instead we were going to do live action videos and have Dylan get stuck in that video as the end twist. They were supposed to be old-fashioned “work safety” videos explaining how to change lightbulbs, and as the quest went on, it became more and more obvious that the maintenance guy in the videos was too aware of what Dylan was doing. This all came out from a one-hour workshop.

There wasn’t really a pitch, but rather a back-and-forth like “could we do a quest about Dylan changing lightbulbs in a ritualistic way? We could have these sentient work safety videos explain how to do it and “Dylan could get trapped inside the video.” Much later, when the live action turned out to be a no-go, we pivoted to the current cartoon instead, and that was even funnier than our initial idea.

#4317. Tomorrow's Battlefield 6 patch somehow makes jets more useless, improves armor bar visibility in Redsec

The first Battlefield 6 patch of the year is almost here, bringing a smattering of changes, including one that doesn't quite make sense.

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

The patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

The other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

Read on below for the 1.1.3.5 change log.

#4315. Heartopia surprise launches on Steam and shockingly, everyone seems to be happy

Heartopia players didn't actually end up having to wait too long to play the game on Steam, which is certainly not what anyone expected.

Heartopia has officially arrived on Steam, only a little over a week after it launched on iOS and Android. When the game’s release date was announced back in December, developer XD said it was pushing back the Steam release without offering any hints about how long the delay was going to be.

While the game can be played on PC through TapTap, the developer’s own emulator, many had been anticipating the Steam launch. So you can imagine that when the free-to-play life sim game surprisingly showed up on Valve’s platform on Saturday, there were a lot of happy people.

Heartopia’s Steam release has, much like mobile launch, been a success. We do know that the game reached the number one spot across app stores in over 50 countries, and though the Steam numbers may not be as record-breaking, everything is looking pretty good.

The game peaked at a decent 28,815 concurrent players (via SteamDB) on Steam one day after it launched, and considering how sticky it has been with the majority of those players so far - and the fact the launch itself was a surprise - there’s every chance those figures will improve over the course of this week as it picks up momentum.

Steam user reviews have similarly been quite positive, with the overall rating currently sitting at Mostly Positive, based on over 1,400 reviews.

You’re still need either a Google, Facebook, or Apple account to log into the game, same as you would on mobile. The Steam version does support cross-play with other platforms, so you’ll be able to play with your friends on mobile.

We’ve been playing a lot of Heartopia ourselves, and have been updating and expanding our guides. If you’re looking to get started, such as with how to add and play with friends, how to regain Energy, and how to unlock home plots, our guides offer the best place to start.

Once you’re past the initial hump, you’ll probably be looking for where to find things like mushrooms, bugs, fish, and birds, so definitely bookmark those, too. If you simply like free stuff, our Heartopia codes page is a must read before playing.
