#4313. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 23, 2026

This week has been home to some disheartening news. BioWare, the creators of games like Mass Effect and Dragon Age, is being shut down amid a flurry of layoffs. It's another frustrating story from a struggling video game industry. Below you will find some of our stories about the legendary developer, including our massive 2016 oral history. And then after that, you can read about our recommendations of what to play this weekend.

I spent the early hours playing Final Fantasy Resonance trying to figure out precisely why I couldn't put it down. I eventually realized that the game manages in a very purposeful way to answer that quiet need I've so frequently had: "I wish I could experience a game just like Final Fantasy IV or VI again, for the first time, but with a new cast and story." That's pretty much what you can expect here; Resonance is a very purposeful throwback experience that harkens to the early days of FF pixel adventures, but with several modern conveniences, graphical flourishes, and depth added into the mix. It's a big and refreshingly wholesome journey of entertaining party members, summoning giant creatures, flying an airship across the world, and fighting turn-based battles that include absurd spell effects. It's one of my favorite games of the year, and well worth the time it will take to explore. Read our full review for more.

Expect to hear a lot of people proclaiming this as "one of the good ones," as Modern Warfare came out swinging this week with a strong campaign, compelling additions to competitive multiplayer, and an impressive extraction shooter mode in the form of DMZ. I've already been impressed by the first few hours of the campaign, which offers a tense, harrowing, and often disturbingly brutal story that bounces between a number of character perspectives. The gunplay feels tuned in, the traversal and melee is satisfying, and the narrative beats grounded in excellent actin performances. Our reviewer has spent even more time with the full game, and can share their full perspective to help inform whether you want to take a dive into this year's installment.

The Nintendo Sports franchise, which began with Wii Sports in 2006, has never been about the single-player experience. That remains true 20 years later in Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. But this time around, Nintendo has boosted the amount of content beyond what the series has typically provided, appealing to all player counts, all while retaining its trademark approachability. Whether you're joining together with three friends for some friendly competition across the package's 12 sports or you're trying to climb the Island Crown ladder by beating increasingly difficult single-player opponents, Switch Sports Resort is a great motion-controlled collection.

Halloween is around the corner. As you’re buying overpriced candy, deciding which version of the Joker to dress up as, and debating between watching Obsession and Backrooms over a cup of cider, it’s the perfect time to replay old horror games or dive into new ones. 2026 has a solid roster of choices for the latter thanks to releases like Resident Evil Requiem, Paranormasight: The Mermaid’s Curse, and Silent Hill: Townfall, but Tenebris Somnia shouldn’t be overlooked if you’re looking for a cool indie throwback.

Part retro-inspired adventure game, part live-action indie horror film, you’ll uncover the mystery of a nightmare-induced apartment building and battle horrors to rescue your trapped ex. The gameplay is survival horror 101, but it’s executed well, with consistently clever and inventive puzzle-solving as a highlight. It may not be a graphical powerhouse, but Tenebris Somnia still maintains a creepy atmosphere thanks to solid scares partly delivered by effective and well-made live-action cinematics. If you’re going to binge horror films, you may as well play one too. You can read my full review here.

Full disclosure: I have not played One Piece: Grand Gourmet. I was trying to finish up Castlevania: Belmont's Curse when a review game landed in my lap that I've had to give my full attention. That said, I have watched a lot of the One Piece anime, have a cat named Nami, and dog named Luffy.

I don't know if One Piece: Grand Gourmet is any good, but I like the premise and pixel graphics. One Piece is a very malleable franchise (which is why its live action adaptation is pretty good), so the idea of managing a restaurant as Sanji feels like it could be a very good fit. I plan on climbing aboard with all my hopes and dreams soon. And it is out now, which is good to know.

Similar to the entry above, I have not yet played Stupid Never Dies yet (there are too many video games!), but we like to use this weekly article to call out the new video games of the week. I am eager to check out Stupid Never Dies primarily because of its pop-punk soundtrack and 2000s aesthetic. I think it has the potential to be a fun, nostalgic throwback to my youth when I was learning Blink-182's "Dammit" on guitar and playing Devil May Cry.

The Blood of Dawnwalker has been out for just over seven weeks now, but I wouldn't blame you if you haven't finished it – or even started it – yet. A lot has come out! But if you need a reason to jump back in, this week's 1.1 update is a great excuse – the devs have added hundreds of bug fixes and other minor improvements, so it should run better than it ever did before. There's also an even easier difficulty mode if you want to cruise through without worrying about combat, and a new in-game potion that lets you respec all your skill points. I stalled out about halfway through (when I started playing Wolverine), but I'm planning to jump back in this weekend.

Oh, and you can pet dogs and cats now. Maybe I should have led with that.

Multiplayer physics mountain-climbing game Peak became one of the most viral co-op experiences of 2025 (I refuse to use the term friendslop), but only PC players have enjoyed its wacky shenanigans. That changed this week as Peak is now available on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Switch 2. Either alone or, preferably, alongside up to three friends, you’ll try to ascend procedurally generated, absurdly unrealistic mountains riddled with dangers. Working together is key, a tricky prospect thanks to the in-game proximity chat that necessitates sticking together, but griefing each other, intentionally or otherwise, is just as entertaining – maddeningly frustrating at times, but entertaining. Peak on consoles includes all post-launch content and, best of all, supports crossplay for all platforms.

The original Azul remains one of my all-time favorite games even after many years, but it just misses the bar with its strategic complexity to be one I'd pull out to play with the kids. That why I was especially delighted to find that Azul Kids is one of those rare "adapted for children" projects that turned out extremely well.

Players take on the roll of creative young artists building mosaic displays with various colored tiles. The concept remains simple enough to work for even very young players of age five or six, but the whole family should have fun with the approachable strategy implications of choosing tiles and completing your masterpiece.

#4312. The Ratchet & Clank Game You Didn’t Know Existed is Shutting Down

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

I’ll admit, I have a tendency to hyperfixate on games and franchises that I care about, occasionally to the detriment of others. Even so, I like to consider myself sufficiently plugged-into this industry, especially when it comes to relatively big-name IPs like the Ratchet & Clank series. You can imagine my distinct confusion, then, when I heard today that Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble was shutting down, to which my response was, “what the heck is Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble?”

Apparently it is, soon to be “was,” a PvP live service shooter available for iOS and Android. The game saw a soft-launch in mid-2025 in limited territories like Canada, France, and parts of Asia, which probably explains why I have literally never heard of it alongside the fact that I don’t often pay much mind to mobile games in general.

In the wake of Destiny 2's upcoming final content update, thousands of of fans have called for Destiny 3 to begin development.

What’s especially interesting about this particular discontinuation, however, is that the game wasn’t even actually finished yet. That soft-launch was as far as the game had ever managed to get, with its planned global launch officially being scrapped and further development ceasing as of the game’s most recent update today, according to its official home page.

As the home page announcement explains, with the newest update pushed out today to mobile storefronts, no further updates for Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble will be released, and on November 21, the game will be pulled from said storefronts entirely.

This is a feature that looks at how live service games are dying as a popular choice in the industry.

For those who are still actively playing the game, you don’t have to stop playing it right away. While new players won’t be able to download the game from the Google Play or Apple App stores anymore following the delisting, anyone who already has the game downloaded will be able to keep playing multiplayer matches until the servers are officially closed in May 2027.

On November 21, the game will be pulled from storefronts entirely.

The game’s “Qwark Pass” seasons will continue running until the server closure, while the game’s “Super Pass” has been made free, with all of its related content now available to earn throughout the remaining seasons. Of course, said content will vanish into the ether once the game goes offline, so whether or not you can be bothered is up to you.

This also goes for any in-app purchases made on things like currency, cosmetics, upgrades, and so forth. If you’re looking to get a refund for any of that, the developers suggest you contact the Apple App Store and Google Play Store’s respective support lines to determine eligibility. Again, absolutely everything is being erased when the servers shutter in May, so whether you want a refund or to keep playing, you’d better act now.

In its final announcement, the developers offered some words of thanks to the players who joined them for the soft-launch process. “On behalf of the dev team and everyone helping to make the game, thanks to our amazing community for all your support, especially to those who have spent time playing, sharing feedback, and helping shape Ranger Rumble throughout its development,” they wrote.

While not as high-profile as some other historic live-service flops over the years, the discontinuation of Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble is another good sign that live-service games are reaching the end of an era. Aside from a very fortunate few that manage to keep attention with consistent updates and player-grabbing content like Fortnite’s One Piece event, the majority end up crashing and burning well before they can take off in earnest.

Sony in particular has been putting the kibosh on live-service games left and right for the last couple of years, mostly following the disastrous launch of Concord, and it seems even its major first-party PlayStation IPs like Ratchet & Clank aren’t safe from the proverbial axe.

Sony Interactive Entertainment executive Hideaki Nishino doubles down on multiplayer investments during a recent Famitsu interview.

#4311. Poll: Will You Be Using Zelda Notes With Ocarina Of Time?

With the Ocarina of Time Switch 2 remake, Nintendo is once again using its Zelda Notes feature via the Nintendo Switch app for mobile.

While I wasn't able to access and test out the app's features during the review period, I've been dabbling quite a bit since Nintendo pushed it live for launch. And y'know what? It's fine.

Just like Zelda Notes for Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, there's nothing here that I'd deem essential to the core experience, but if you're after some harmless supplemental material, it does the job.

My favourite feature? Gossip Quests. Provided you've activated Zelda Notes within Ocarina of Time's settings, you can link your phone directly to the software to partake in a little game to hunt down specific locations depicted in photos. Doing so will earn you points, which you can eventually spend on new ocarina songs.

To be clear, these ocarina songs won't unlock anything in-game, but you can access a playable ocarina in the app and learn the songs yourself, tapping and holding the on-screen holes to perform a variety of tunes.

It's surprisingly tricky, and in an amusing turn of events, pressing three holes at once also acted as a screenshot tool for my phone, so I had to go ahead and delete that function in my phone settings.

You can also come up with your own, original songs and share them via QR code. I haven't come up with anything I'd deem even remotely enjoyable for anyone else, but it's a cool little feature. [For the authentic Ocarina experience circa 1998, I need The Simpsons theme, stat! - Ed.]

Once unlocked in the game, you can also view enemies from the Hall of Fallen Foes. The app also provides a wealth of stats, including daily records, and you can also consult maps if you're gunning for 100% completion and test your Ocarina of Time knowledge with quizzes.

Again, it's fine. There are features, like the Gossip Quests, that would have been awesome had they been included in the game itself in some way, and we'd recommend at least giving it a go if you're looking to extend your playtime. (Fingers crossed for a Master Quest update!)

#4310. Battlefield 6’s first big map in months is coming to Labs soon, but I'm more excited about BF4's Golmud Railway making its way to BF6

As promised, Battlefield Labs is coming back to bring us a preview of some of Battlefield 6’s upcoming Season 2 content.

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it plans to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a big component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the new maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios says the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

The blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of big maps as Battlefield 6 currently is.

Another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. Interestingly, there appears to be some sort of mechanic unique to Contaminated that the developer also wants to evaluate.

More Labs sessions are planned, including one that will show off new gameplay tools and vehicles. The AH-6 Little Bird helicopter was specifically namedropped, which makes sense given that it’s going to be part of Season 2’s content.

Battlefield Labs sessions will also extend beyond the biggest-ticket items of maps and vehicles. BF Studios said we should expect tests of upcoming features, like the Aircraft Radar, as part of a list of other air combat updates.

Ground vehicles, and they way the various rockets interact with them, will also be evaluated in a different session, with specific adjustments planned for RPGs and TOWs. And, of course, the work to improve and perfect hit reg remains ongoing, and future tweaks will go through Labs first.

There’s even more exciting news for fans of big maps, as the blog post also confirmed that Battlefield 4’s Golmud Railway is currently in the works, planned to go live in a future season. Golmud Railway will show up early in Labs, and you can expect it to evolve over multiple sessions.

For context, when it does arrive in Battlefield 6, Golmud Railway will be the largest map in the game, which is saying something. Though the map is beloved by vehicle players, it has its issues elsewhere, and BF Studios says it will be looking at all that when it creates the BF6, emphasising that it won’t be a simple port of the BF4 original.

Finally, the post throws a bone to Redsec battle royale players still waiting for a Solo mode. BF Studios continues to test the idea internally, but it’s taking a while. Needless to say, there are so many aspects that need to be considered. Game pace, balance, player survivability, match flow just to name a few.

Redsec BR was built with squads in mind, so that task is extra challenging. Though the developer didn’t say when we can expect Solos to arrive in Labs, players will get a chance to experience it before it enters the live game.

#4309. Gods & Demons tier list - From best to worst heroes

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version: 3.0.10

If you're wondering who the best heroes are, our Gods & Demons tier list will surely come in handy. Each of the heroes specialises in something - be it healing, tanking, or dealing damage - and if you want to have a strong team that can take on every stage in the game, this is the place to be.

I've ranked every single hero, so you will have a clear idea of who you should be using on your team.  About Gods & Demons tier list I have to mention that although I've also ranked the Epic and below heroes, most of them are all in the lowest tier. The reasoning for that is that you will not use any of them once you get the Mythic heroes. You will probably still use one Legendary (maybe, maybe not?), but the Epics and below you will use just for the Codex and as fodder.

I recommend upgrading the heroes at the top of this Gods & Demons tier list because those are the strongest at the moment.

Most of the time, you can make any hero work, as long as the team has a decent synergy. However, you will also need to ascend them, so dupes are good. Getting dupes for your Mythic heroes is not that easy, which is why sometimes you will use Legendary heroes (or Epic in worst-case scenarios).

Which are the best heroes in Gods & Demons? There are a handful of heroes who could be considered the overall "best" right now, but in my opinion, you can make most Mythic heroes work. You can try out various comps to make your team shine, and if something doesn't work how you want it to, then go for something different!

The best part is you can reset your heroes - to do that, all you have to do is hit the Rebirth button, and the hero you've upgraded will be reset to level 1.

Now it's time to dive into our Gods & Demons tier list!

Since the game has been removed from both App Store and Play Store, we won't keep updating this tier list anymore.

Blade Sentinel - Orpheus is hands-down the best hero at the moment. He can deal AoE damage, and once he reaches 50% (at first level, then 60% and then 70%), he becomes a powerhouse. He is worth upgrading and using once you get him.

Goddess of Light - Ostara is the best healer you can have right now. She can mitigate damage, heal, buff her allies' ATK and Crit, and even when she dies, she grants additional healing and buffs.

Indestructible Power King - Grox is one of my favourite heroes. He is the best tank in the game, and he can even taunt enemies. He can curse enemies to take additional damage after two turns, and he is incredibly tanky. He can even revive once per battle!

Nature's Wrath - Freni is a magic DPS who deals incredible AoE damage. She can also bleed enemies and apply Silence if they already have bleed, so depending on the team you have, she can have amazing synergy (with other heroes that also apply bleed) if you manage to silence-lock your opponents.

Resurrection Angel - Seraphel is great if you want to revive your fallen allies. She can also heal the team, making her an absolute beast. She is not as good as Goddess of Light - Ostara, but if you don't have Ostara, she is an outstanding pick.

Celestial Maiden - Liana is another great support who can offer heals, buffs, and CC resist to allies, which makes her top-tier for the Arena. She can also dispel debuffs, and if you manage to upgrade her Soaring Dance to level 3, she will also gain DMG Reflection. An absolute beast for the Arena!

Tribe Guardian - Ella can deal AoE true damage to the enemies, which is a pretty good skill, especially for the story mode. I have been using her since she was the first Mythic I pulled, and she is great. With the right team, she could even be S tier or above.

Blade Assassin - Rein is great with the right team. He can trigger additional normal attacks when allies hit the enemy, and he deals increased damage to targets with lower HP.

Sylvan Spirit - Luna is a Legendary hero, but her kit is quite good. She can apply HP Regen to multiple allies, on top of a flat heal, and she can also dispel debuffs. If you don't have any better healers, she will do great early to mid-game.

I strongly advise against using any of the heroes in the B tier for longer than you have to. Even though we have Mythic heroes here, they pale in comparison to any of the heroes ranked in A tier or above.

For instance, Sand Fury - Billy has a powerful shielding ability, but it only provides shields to two allies. He applies with his Enormous Physique a shield to all allies at the start of battle, but it is not that great.

As for Hell's Roar - Grom, he is a DPS and has Lifesteal, but it is not that great. He cannot self-sustain enough in the later stages, so it's best to just pick a better hero.

Do not use any of the heroes from the bottom of this Gods and Demons tier list for your teams. Their main purpose is to be either dismantled or used to ascend your main characters. The ones you will find in this tier are all of the Epic rarity and below, which is of no use for any of the game's content. Once you unlock them in your Codex, that's it. Move on.

We also have a Angel Legion tier list which ranks every girl in the game with a similar theme to this one and a GFL 2 tier list that also features girls. You might be interested in both!

#4308. Phantom Blade Zero Review In Progress – Shaping Up To Be One Of The Best Action Games I've Ever Played

Phantom Blade Zero is an astounding achievement for the action genre. So astounding that I feel pulled to experience everything it has to offer… and that means instead of rolling credits, I’ve been busy completing story-critical side quests and more to get the most complete ending. That’s another way of saying I am enjoying this game very, very much but still need more time to render a final verdict, which is why you’re reading a review-in-progress of Phantom Blade Zero rather than a scored piece.

Though I’m not interested in guesstimating a score right now, I know it will be high because Phantom Blade Zero impresses and then some. It is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and I’m shocked to be writing that. This is a debut of sorts for developer S-Game, which has dabbled in mobile games and smaller-scale titles; it’s the team’s first triple-A release, and its first game of this kind. This studio is so clearly a dedicated student of the genre, analyzing what works here and what works there in other action greats to create something of its own. It looks forward at what action games can do, can play like, can look like, while looking back at the games before it and understanding why those games – games like Devil May Cry, Elden Ring, Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, Bayonetta, and just about every other quality action game you can think of – continue to be ones we hold so highly. Should it stick the landing, Phantom Blade Zero will join that echelon of action pedigree.

Protagonist Soul is a quiet, mostly stoic martial arts master who prefers to let his blades (of which there are so, so many) do the talking. The Order he’s sworn his life to betrays him, and, in an effort to right wrongs, he discovers a villainous conspiracy to seize full power of the blood-soaked Chinese martial underground known as Wulin. As a result, puppets, secret sects, powerful god-like creatures, monstrous beasts, and much more prowl Wulin’s various biomes. I haven’t kept count, but there are a massive number of enemies to take down, both standard mob variants and bosses, and the game stays fresh throughout. It's even fresher when you consider how many weapons you can acquire on Soul’s journey.

Every weapon is wholly unique, like picking up a new character in a fighting game, each with its own moveset and abilities. Upgrading these weapons through various tiers unlocks additional abilities, and you can even Soul Temper weapons to add one final, game-changing ability or perk. A fully upgraded weapon can have a moveset that uses the majority of buttons on your controller. You can do the same with Phantom Edges, special tide-turning weapons with limited uses (before you build up additional charges). Combined with different accessories and medicine types, Phantom Blade Zero offers hundreds, perhaps thousands, of combat kit permutations. You can play as a drunken fighter who switches between sober, tipsy, and drunken states, with his range and damage output changing as a result; you can focus on a bleed build, ripping enemies to shreds with charged attacks that utilize Soul's own HP to deal extra damage (that can then be earned back with bleed); you can use lightning, wind, fire, and ice to create elemental storms against enemies, and you can use a sword that switches between different elemental states on command as well. You can also just pound enemies to pulp with Phantom Edge fists, too. I’ve struggled to stop using these fists since acquiring them because they’re so satisfying.

Forty-plus hours into Phantom Blade Zero, it feels like I’ve played as dozens of different Souls because I've discovered so many build types. S-Game smartly pushes you to try new builds and weapons as you get them, doling out generous upgrade materials and currency; it encourages you to try everything, and the next weapon might just become your new favorite.

Finding these materials (and additional fights) is great fun, too, because Phantom Blade Zero’s various open-area biomes are a genuine joy to explore. You are always rewarded for taking the optional path, and those rewards are always worthwhile. You might find a healthy pile of upgrade materials, or a boss with a weapon you’ll fall in love with. The way buildings, alleys, caves, cliffsides, and other environmental features weave in and out of each other evokes FromSoftware’s architectural design and the subsequent shortcut “aha!” moments.

That said, Phantom Blade Zero is definitively not a Soulslike, though you’d be forgiven for assuming as much given its challenging suite of bosses, interconnected world, and Phantom Bell checkpoints, which are this game’s equivalent of bonfires. However, its challenge is much more surmountable (with various difficulties and accessories to ease parry and dodge timing), and its world progression is materially different. Kill an enemy and it’s dead for good, which to my surprise, adds a sense of worldbuilding I didn’t know I wanted. Progression through this journey feels tangible because I’m actually removing traces of evil with my weapons, traces that don’t respawn when I interact with checkpoints. It’s a nice change of pace that narratively speaks to Soul’s efforts.

Along the way, countless reading materials shed light on Phantom Blade Zero’s intertwining stories, and tracking down the next memory, scroll, or book entry rewards you if you’re interested in the full picture of this Wuxia story. I’d argue the game’s story is its weakest element, but only when compared to the rest of the package. It doesn't break any new ground narratively, but it provides enough mystery and thrill to keep things moving. And while performances are great, talking to characters is still mostly just two people standing across from each other talking through a new quest. Fortunately, cutscenes pick up the slack with dramatic villains, heartfelt revelations, raw tension, and more.

Production value is high across the board, thanks to incredibly impressive animation and a beautiful rendering of this dark fantasy China. Faces are lifelike, nudging up just shy of the uncanny valley as close-ups reveal porous details, lip quivers, and more, bringing an excellent cast of Chinese performances to life. The English voice acting has its standouts, but Soul’s voice is boring, so I highly recommend the Chinese vocals.

Boss fights draw clear inspiration from Chinese cinema and boast a wondrous sense of awe and scale that only the best in the genre typically offer. There are a ton of bosses, too, with very few repeats (repeats do happen in segmented challenge trials), and it’s impressive to think back on just how many I defeated, and just how many of them delivered a unique fight. I appreciate the checkpoints between boss phases as well. There are so many bosses – nearing 100 or more if I had to guess – and having my progression saved through phases removes some of the repetition I often feel when, say, phase two of a boss continues to kill me and I have to blitz through phase one again and again before taking another stab at it.

That scale and on-screen excitement carry through almost every fight in the game, down to even the simplest mob fights, though these are starting to feel a touch repetitive as I’m barreling toward the game’s end. Soul moves like the world’s greatest martial artist, but your controller inputs make it happen. If you mash the attack button, it looks nice… but if you use each weapon’s prescribed inputs and abilities, Phantom Blade Zero delivers a level of detailed action I’ve seen in few other games. You direct the game’s action, and this lets you turn what might otherwise be just another group of fodder enemies into an electric bout of spectacle.

To say I greatly enjoy this game greatly undersells my feelings – writing this review-in-progress is frustrating because I want to get back to Phantom Blade Zero. I expect to reach credits in the coming days, so please be on the lookout for my final verdict this week.

#4307. Arc Raiders finally reveals early 2026 roadmap, but we’re not getting a new map for a while

The first couple of months of 2026 in the world of Arc Raiders look pretty promising, but the big guns are being held back for now.

After weeks of waiting, Arc Raiders developer Embark has officially unveiled the first few months of the game’s 2026 roadmap. The plan is split into four months, covering January to April, collectively dubbed Escalation.

We’re expecting a content update each month, with the majority of the biggest additions happening on the game’s existing maps. There is, however, at least one new map in the works, but it won’t be here until sometime in April.

While we wait for that, Arc Raiders is going to go through several events and other in-game changes, some more meaningful (and exciting) than others. January looks to be the lightest so far, which makes sense given that it’s just a week or so from ending.

January’s chapter is titled Headwinds, kicking off on January 27. This segment will see the addition of a new matchmaking option for players above level 40 - at or near the game’s endgame. We’re also expecting a new Map Condition, and a new Player Project for everyone to contribute to.

Things start getting interesting in February, when Shrouded Sky will begin. This chapter brings three exciting additions to Arc Raiders. There will be a new Map Condition, new Arc Threat, and the start of another Player Project.

Interestingly, we’re going to see some sort of map update during the month, but Embark didn’t share anymore details. The next Raider Deck will also deploy in February, alongside a new Expedition Window.

The Flashpoint chapter begins in March, when we’re expecting another new Map Condition, one more new Arc Threat, as well as another Player Project. March’s most interesting addition is an update to everyone’s trusty rooster friend, Scrappy.

Finally, April is when the big guns come out, because that’s when the first new map of 2026 will arrive in Arc Raiders. With it, comes a new large Arc, which is to be expected. A new Map Condition will debut then, too, likely starting off on the new map.

That’s pretty much it, but seeing as we’re just one day away from the start of the January stage, things are about to get exciting again in Arc Raiders.

#4306. Demian Saga tier list and a reroll guide

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version: 1.6.3

Do you want to know who the best heroes are in Demian Saga? Then look no further, because I've written this Demian Saga tier list to give you all the information you need about which heroes to reroll for, and which aren't worth your time.

This lovely Android RPG has quite a lot of heroes, and while a lot of them can become UL, not all of them are as strong as you might think. Below, I've ranked them all, so you know exactly which select few are worth keeping, and when it's time to reroll for an optimal start. Demian Saga Factions First things first - there are a few affinities that, when paired together, can provide some bonus effects to your team. So, ideally, you want to do exactly that. These are the affinities in Demian Saga:

There is also a Neutral affinity, which can pair with each of the others.

Personality Chemistry You can also gain additional effects from the hero's personality, so depending on which personality they have, you can get either Penetrate Physical Defense, Resist Physical Penetration, Penetrade Magical Defense, or Resist Magical Penetration. Sometimes it's best to change up your team a little depending on which enemy you're facing.

To activate some of these effects, you need to pick either 2, 3, 4, or 5 heroes belonging to the same personality. They include:

Of course, considering all of these bonus effects, you can mix and match a few of them depending on which heroes you're using on your team. Ideally, you want to go for a team that has good synergy in terms of skills (first and foremost), and then focus on the bonus effects (this comes second).

Now that we've got this out of the way, let's check out our complete Demian Saga tier list, as well as the reroll guide! SS Tier  |  S Tier  |  A Tier  |  B Tier  |  C Tier

Grave is one of the best DPS heroes in Demian Saga right now, hence his place on our tier list. He has AoE damage and can also debuff enemies. He's one of the best heroes you can reroll for at the moment.

When it comes to magic damage, Manes is a beast. She not only deals lots of it but also grants a barrier to allies, buffing their Magic DEF. To top it all off, she can debuff enemies, making her a great addition to a magic team.

All of Cynthia's skills are AoE, and she can inflict lots of negative effects on the enemies. You can inflict crowd control effects with her, such as Freeze and Frostbite, which makes her a great addition to many teams.

Gekkou is a great melee Physical attacker who can inflict knockback on enemies. She is also able to buff herself with a stealth effect, making her untargetable by opponents.

With an amazing kit, Slayer is a beast in terms of damage, buffs, and debuffs. She can become invincible, she can knockback enemies, and to top it all off, she can make them vulnerable too.

Princesa is a mix of support-tank-damage dealer, which makes her a pretty good hero. She can buff her evasion after using Radiant Blessing, and with Shield of Justice, she can protect the allies around her.

Bianca is a support who can pull enemies together with her Gravity skill, and reduce the affected enemy's movement speed. She can also remove all the enemy buffs, and reduce their Accuracy, making her a good member of a team with lots of Evasion-focused heroes.

King Arthur can buff his and his allies' Attack Speed, and his skills can unleash a rapid flurry of hits. He is a decent damage dealer, but he is most useful thanks to his Defense Burst skill.

With Serena Claro's kit, you can debuff and free enemies all around. She can deal good AoE damage, which freezes enemies and applies frostbite, and with Ice Shield, she can pretty much keep enemies at bay.

Judas is okay, but sadly not good enough to be higher on our Demian Saga tier list. He can buff his Evasion temporarily, and also his Physical DEF and ATK. Sadly, the ATK won't come in handy too much, since his damage is not that high, regardless.

Elizabeth can buff allies' Accuracy, which is good against enemies with a lot of Evasion. She can also remove buffs from opponents and silence them, dealing decent damage and inflicting more crowd control in the form of knockback and frostbite.

Bibiane Chain can stun enemies, inflict knockdown, and shock them too. She has a lot of negative effects/crowd control in her kit, but her damage is a little lacking unless she's fully maxed out.

All the heroes in this tier are highly underwhelming, so investing in them is not worth it at all. Even though a couple of them are SL rarity, their kit is lacklustre at best - as for the rest, they are either too low rarity (the R ones) or are just going to fall off pretty quickly.

I strongly advise you not to use them in your team, unless you have nothing better at the moment. You shouldn't even have them if you reroll, or at least you should have way better options. If you haven't rerolled yet, check out the next page to learn how to reroll in Demian Saga.

Rerolling in Demian Saga is extremely easy. However, there is not a lot of need for too much rerolling (in my opinion, at least), because you will get one SL-rarity hero by default, and it's one that you can reroll infinitely until you get your desired one. Here is how to reroll in Demian Saga: Step 1 - Play through the tutorial until you get to Chapter 1-9. That's where you unlock the Recruit option.

Step 2 - Do the single Recruit and pick one of the top-tier characters in the game. Here you can reroll or re-do the recruit as many times as you want, until you get your desired hero. Step 3 - Claim all of the rewards in your mailbox. You will get a lot of stuff, including summon tickets and Gems that you can use to pull a few more times. Step 4 - Go summon! If you got the heroes you wanted, then go ahead and bind your account. If you didn't, then proceed to the next step. Step 5 - Tap on Settings -> Account -> Withdraw -> Withdraw (to confirm it). This option will delete your game data, and then all you have to do is start over.

And that wraps up our Demian Saga tier list. We hope you found it helpful! While you're here, check out our Demian Saga codes article so you can snag yourself some free in-game goodies.

#4305. Nioh 3’s generous demo is out now, and your progress carries over to the full game

If you’re looking for a way to check out one of the biggest releases of early 2026, Team Ninja has made it easy for you.

Nioh 3 is one of the most anticipated games of 2026, and it’s easily among the biggest releases of February. We’re a few days away from the start of that month, however, but we don’t have to wait until then to actually play Team Ninja’s next major release.

The previously announced demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.

Unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game. This is pretty new for the series, which has typically launched first on PlayStation before coming to PC months later.

The Nioh 3 demo includes a decent portion of content from the beginning of the game. It’s enough to show off the core duality mechanic, letting you switch between the Samurai and Ninja styles at will. It also includes a preview of the game’s open field level design, which makes it sit somewhere between full open world and the more linear level design of past Nioh games.

Feedback from the previous beta has been implemented into the demo (and full release), so you may see some familiar faces, as well as areas you visited before - assuming you played that one.

Another big reason why you might want to grab the Nioh 3 demo is that your progress in it will carry over to the full version. This includes the character creator, too, meaning you can spend all day perfecting your character without having to worry about missing out on playing the actual game.

The demo even supports online multiplayer for up to three players, in case you come to Nioh for co-op. If you complete the available content, you’ll earn an in-game bonus in the full version. This is something Team Ninja has done with past Nioh titles, of course.

This time, your reward is the Twin-Snake Helmet. Just make sure you complete the demo before February 15.

Nioh 3 is out February 6 on PC, and PlayStation 5.

#4304. Report: Ghost Of Yōtei Developer Sucker Punch Hit With Layoffs

Sucker Punch, the team behind Ghost of Yōtei, Ghost of Tsushima, Infamous, and Sly Cooper, has been hit with layoffs, according to a report by Aftermath. The outlet states that 26 roles have been affected as the studio prepares its next project.

Aftermath cites a former Sucker Punch employee who confirmed the number of layoffs. The outlet also obtained a company email announcing the staff cuts.

“After carefully observing the challenges in the market and reviewing the team needs for our next project, we've decided to make some staffing reductions. Several positions across Sucker Punch will be eliminated as a result,” reads a section of the email. Sucker Punch then says it will work to support affected staff in their transition and will share more details next week about what comes next. The studio has not yet publicly commented on the layoffs.

This news comes a few weeks after the release of the Complete Edition of Ghost of Yōtei, which originally launched in 2025 to critical and commercial success. The release coincided with the arrival of two substantial DLCs: the story expansion Echoes of Sekigahara and a roguelike mode called Most Wanted that reintroduces Ghost of Tsushima hero Jin Sakai as a playable character.

#4303. 8 Best Anime Where Tiny Details Become Major Story Revelations

Usama Mehmood is a Senior Writer at DualShockers with more than five years of experience in the video game industry. He has been writing professionally since 2021 and covering games since 2022, with work spanning guides, lists, reviews, and features across action-adventure games, JRPGs, open-world titles, racing games,

You know, I’ve rewatched certain anime scenes more times than I’d like to admit on YT or just browsing social media, and it's almost never for the big moments. It’s usually for something small: a character’s hand hovering a half-second too long or a line of dialogue that sounded like filler. Then, twenty episodes later, the show unexpectedly turns that one detail into the thing that rewrites almost everything you thought you knew about it.

Watched These Once? These 8 Anime Hit Harder the Second Time Around

It’s like that foreshadowing or missing puzzle piece coming back later that just makes you bewildered for a second or two at the show’s ingenious attention-to-detail, or, well, certain parts of it, to be exact. It made rewatches feel like detective work, and it also makes you appreciate how much patience and planning go into a story that pays off its smallest choices.

So this anime list is for the shows that reward that kind of attention, especially the ones where you can catch the smallest details and understand why they become so prevalent later, during the climax. Naturally, there are lots of spoilers ahead for the discussed anime, so watch out!

It’s funny that I recommended this show to a friend who went into Higurashi expecting a wholesome slice-of-life show, only to regret trusting my recommendation. It's a horror show that takes some characters’ quirks and uses them as pivotal anchors in later episodes.

Take the first arc, for instance: when Keiichi starts scratching his throat, you get the impression that it's a nervous habit. A few arcs later, you realize it’s the first symptom of the Hinamizawa Syndrome, which explains why people who were perfectly friendly suddenly turn on each other.

The twins are another example. See, you know Mion and Shion Sonozaki look nearly identical, and the show plays with that on purpose, but once you know how the identity swap works, you start to doubt every earlier scene where “Mion” seemed slightly off. I can get why some people think this show is straight-up torture, but don’t knock it till you try, am I right?

Let me preface this by saying we don’t argue between Aronofsky’s Black Swan and Satoshi Kon’s Perfect Blue; I love both. This cult-favorite anime movie’s best trick is how it plays with your sense of what’s real. Mima’s decision to quit her pop group CHAM! and become an actress feels like a simple career move, but as you watch, the film shows how every “step forward” she takes strips away a piece of her.

The tiny, uneasy moments, like her flinching at the fax of the Double Bind script or the way her reflection starts reacting a half-beat late, are the film silently telling you that Mima isn’t in control of her own image anymore. And that’s one of the key reasons I adore this movie, even after all these years since I first watched it.

These anime plot twists flipped entire stories on their heads.

On a first watch, Madoka Magica looks like a bright, pastel magical girl series… until you rewatch it and realize it was telling you exactly how it would break your heart from the very first episode. Almost everything in the show, from the unusual designs of the Witch's Labyrinths to the seemingly innocent conversations with Kyubey, carries far more meaning than it initially lets on to you.

I mean, for crying out loud, the show's opening, with its seemingly disconnected imagery and Madoka chasing after a mysterious figure, becomes much more meaningful once you understand what's really happening. Even small character choices carry weight. Mami’s tea parties, her loneliness, and her insistence on keeping up the cheerful senpai act are all easy to read as charm early on in this show.

Now I’ll be very real with you all here; Odd Taxi looks like a quiet slice-of-life show about a walrus cab driver named Hiroshi Odokawa, and it’s hard to say anything about it without spoiling it. He’s a dry, awkward man who talks in deadpan dad jokes and likes listening to a comedy podcast between fares.

Then a missing girl, a yakuza fixer, an idol group, a struggling comedian, and a nurse with a secret all begin orbiting his cab. What looks like a pile of unrelated conversations turns out to be a tightly built puzzle, and almost every piece of it was planted in the very first episodes.

Early on, much of the dialogue feels like filler, with passengers rambling about their lives or Odokawa making small talk, until you later realize this throwaway stuff sets up most of the plot because a casual remark about a missing person, an offhand comment about someone’s job, or even a name dropped once in passing can fill in the main structure of the mystery. The show trusts you to notice, and it rewards you.

Dive into anime with controversial endings with modern shockers like Death Note and classics such as Evangelion.

Everyone knew this was going to be here, and it deserves it even if it's an obvious pick for this list. Death Note is an anime practically built around the idea that the smallest details can make the biggest difference.

What starts as a straightforward cat-and-mouse game between Light and L quickly becomes an elaborate battle of deduction, manipulation, and psychological warfare, where a seemingly insignificant action can expose someone's entire plan.

Whether it's L noticing the peculiarities of Kira's early killings or Light carefully manipulating the Death Note’s rules, the show constantly rewards those who pay attention. It's incredibly satisfying to watch everything click into place, and while the latter half isn’t everyone’s favorite for obvious reasons, the finale is genuinely one of the most memorable endings in the entire anime medium.

I might be biased for including this because Steins;Gate is genuinely one of my favorite anime of all time, and just a few months ago in August, I had the chance to review the Steins;Gate Reboot VN—and the entire thing was just as good as I remembered.

It starts as a quirky science-fiction adventure about a group of eccentric friends experimenting with a microwave, then accidentally stumbles into a conspiracy-theory time-travel adventure that gradually becomes one of the most intricately woven narratives in the medium. I know that sounds like a mouthful, but anyone who’s seen the show will know the series is just like that in terms of writing.

The genius is in how casually the show introduces certain characters, conversations, messages, and seemingly throwaway moments before revealing just how important they are to the bigger picture at the very end, or just when a certain pocket watch strikes 7:35 PM. Sorry, had to do it.

Look, we’re not even going to get into the debate about how the show ended, so this will focus strictly on Attack on Titan’s brilliant foreshadowing, which led to major story revelations and more twists, as my listicle’s title already suggests.

No matter what you think of his directional choices for the last act, Isayama has an incredible knack for planting seemingly insignificant details throughout the story. Things like the truth behind the Walls, the mystery surrounding Eren's basement, and the peculiar behavior of certain Titans initially seem like separate mysteries, but eventually come together in ways that completely change your understanding of the world in later seasons.

Even ordinary moments in both the manga and anime involving characters like Reiner, Bertholdt, and Annie become far more interesting once you pay attention to their behavior or dialogue, since they ultimately foreshadow their twists.

Naoki Urasawa is one of the most legendary manga auteurs with a wide range of back-to-back bangers under his umbrella, but his work in Monster is honestly one of the best things you’ll ever get to see, as long as you’re patient enough.

This slow-burn psychological thriller is the kind of story where an innocent conversation or a character's seemingly insignificant memory can carry far more weight than you initially realize. Even some of the twists thrown in here at times can recontextualize things you've already witnessed in previous episodes, making them feel completely different when you look back at them.

The mystery surrounding Johan, the Kinderheim 511 experiments, and the disturbing picture-book stories are all excellent examples of how Urasawa plants little breadcrumbs throughout the narrative before gradually revealing their significance.

From One Piece's grand treasure to Itachi's tragic illness, these unsolved anime mysteries leave fans guessing.

#4301. Grammy Award-Winning Composer Austin Wintory Shares His Early Musical Drafts Intended For Mass Effect 5

Last week, EA shut down Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer BioWare, which resulted in the cancellation of the fifth Mass Effect game that was announced in 2020. As the fallout from this closure settles, famed video game composer Austin Wintory has shared that he'd been working on a potential soundtrack for the now-canceled game and has publicly released early versions of this score.

In a Bluesky thread, Wintory, who has composed soundtracks for games such as Journey, Sword of the Sea (for which he won a Grammy), Assassin’s Creed: Syndicate, and The Banner Saga trilogy, writes, “Mass Effect was my ultimate white whale, my all-time dream project. For the last couple years I'd been in discussion w/ BioWare & EA to take on the project & as part of that I wrote close to 20 minutes of music to explore where the franchise can go next, may as well share it!"

Wintory uploaded a 20-minute video consisting of eight tracks to his YouTube channel. The video begins with a message further elaborating on the partnership between BioWare, EA, and him. “For the past several years, I’d been in dialogue with people both at BioWare and EA to potentially jump into Mass Effect 5. As part of these conversations, I decided to surprise the team by writing/recording a gigantic love letter to the franchise, with my idea of where it can go next.”

Wintory adds that he composed the music in 2025 and that he “knew nothing” about what Mass Effect 5's story entailed when he did. As such, he describes the music as “narratively speculative.” He adds that this conceptual soundtrack was a direct homage to Jack Wall and Sam Hulick’s soundtrack on the first Mass Effect “while leaning even harder on true analog synths, and a more complex integration of the orchestra (almost akin to the hybrid nature of The Matrix),” he writes. Each music track features a message by Wintory explaining his inspiration for its production.

“Receiving the news alongside everyone else that EA had decided to not only cancel the project but shutdown BioWare entirely was a deeply felt loss," Wintory writes in the video's description. "It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever. Thank you nonetheless to everyone at BioWare and EA's music department for gifting me the chance to dream in your sandbox. It was a privilege to do even that much.”

Wintory's music is the latest piece of potential Mass Effect 5 content to emerge since BioWare’s closure. A day after the shutdown announcement, an unreleased but reportedly legitimate cinematic trailer for the canceled Mass Effect leaked online.

#4300. Quantic Dream addresses toxicity, tech bugs and tutorials for Spellcasters Chronicles closed beta 2 - here's how to get a key

Here are the start and end times for the second Spellcasters Chronicles closed beta, as well as what's new in this latest test.

Quantic Dream has opened up its upcoming fantasy MOBA for a second closed beta weekend starting from today, January 29, until 9AM UTC on Monday February 2.

The closed beta is for PC only in Europe, Asia and North America and potential players can register to join the waitlist for a key at the game’s official website or on the Spellcasters Chronicles Steam page. Players who had access to the first closed beta will automatically have access to the second, but you can sign up on both the site and Steam to increase your chances of entry.

The MOBA genre is competitive in every sense and Quantic Dream is trying to break into it with a Magic the Gathering-esque spin on the format. Players build a deck of cards before queuing into teams of 3, then face off as battling mages, summoning creatures, building fortifications and casting spells rather than choosing a Hero with unique abilities in the traditional MOBA style.

Beta content includes a new map, 6 new spells and 5 new summon creatures for your deck, as well as 3 new buildings too.

Also new for this second closed beta is an introduction and tutorial for some of the game’s finer details, as well as a text chat for strategising and much-needed player reporting system to go with it. It will also feature early versions of the Spellcaster customisation system and ranked matches.

Quantic Dream has said that this closed beta places a strong emphasis on performance, memory usage and overall gameplay stability to create a smoother experience, so with that in mind, here are the minimum and recommended PC specs:

Spellcasters Chronicles is the first ever multiplayer online game from Quantic Dream, the French studio best known for cinematic narrative games like Detroit: Become Human, Heavy Rain and Beyond: Two Souls.

A TV adaptation of the latter game is reportedly in development, or the rights for one have been acquired at least. Elsewhere, Quantic Dream’s long-rumoured game in the Star Wars franchise was revealed as Star Wars Eclipse, a return-to-type narrative action game set in the High Republic era of a galaxy far, far away.

#4298. Infinity Nikki ushers in the Year of the Horse with... a deer-themed Version 2.2

Chromatic Beings Everbright, the latest major Infinity Nikki update, has arrived, bringing Chinese New Year celebrations vibe to the game.

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, open-world dress-up RPG, has delivered yet another big content drop in the form of Chromatic Beings Everbright. The latest update brings the game up to version 2.2, and introduces a new narrative chapter, and gameplay taking place around a festival narrative.

If you couldn’t guess already, the new theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.

The big new story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm. This deceptively serene and blissful region hides a dark secret, however. Chromafaces, the mythical inhabitants of the realm, have to embody fixed identities that dictate how they live and work.

These are doled out through Character Tokens, which are used to assign roles to each individual. The story follows Nikki as she uncovers the script that runs the realm and the facade it props up. Nikki will help free Chromafaces and dispel the illusion.

The Wanxiang Realm is split into three areas. Cai Ye is your typical lantern-lit district, where festivals and fireworks happen. Kongming Gorge is almost the opposite of that; a quiet and cold place. Finally, Jiuhua Pavilion literally floats above the region, and it's home to neverending music and dance.

The other big addition in 2.2 are the two new 5-Star Resonance Outfits with some interesting gameplay implications. Where Wanxiang Weaves Life is inspired by wuxia aesthetics, and true to its inspirations, it lets Nikki shapeshift into different Spirit Personas - and automatically collect resources in her vicinity.

Chroma's Mortal Heart, on the other hand, allows Nikki to fly around the Wanxiang Realm, drawing on the power of the Celestial Deer. This outfit also uses Celestial Deer Vision to automatically ping and mark treasure chests around her.

You can also look forward to Nefarious Shadows, a new Ability Outfit, which lets Nikki see through disguises, and reveals hidden paths in the world.

As with every major update, of course, there are themed activities and limited-time events throughout. Hotpot House is a cooking minigame where you attempt to run the eponymous restaurant, whereas Flavor Frenzy is series of platforming challenges that tasks you with gathering ingredients. Fortune Mahjong is a little more straightforward, with support for solo and multiplayer play.

If you’re jumping back into the game soon, be sure to hit up our Infinity Nikki codes page for some freebies.

#4297. Captain Tsubasa Ace tier list of football players

Making a strong team is not a trivial task, as you will have to pick the best footballers in the game, and this tier list should help you pick the right ones.

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version: 1.9.0

Based on their performance, we have ranked all of the footballers in Captain Tsubasa Ace in tiers from S to B. If you are new to this game and want to know the best options for your team, you will find all the answers here!

Based on the popular manga/anime, Captain Tsubasa offers a more arcadey approach compared to the traditional football games that we grew to love. If you are an older gamer (like, really old!), it will remind you of the days at the arcades, where you used to spend your coins to play games like Soccer Superstars. Of course, with the addition of modern graphics and a lot more options in general.

About Captain Tsubasa Ace tier list The following list reflects my view on the current meta. I considered several things when I came up with these rankings. Players' stats and skills are the main factors, but also the available options. Currently, there are many more MF and FW players than GK, for example. That said, there's no absolute tier list. If you enjoy a certain player and can perform with them, that's good enough!

With that out of the way, let's get right into our Captain Tsubasa Ace tier list!

These are the best footballers currently in Captain Tsubasa Ace, thus, I've put them at the top of the tier list. I have to make a special mention of Shingo Takasugi and Shinji Sanada because even though they are only SR rarity, their performance is amazing.

A-Tier players are certainly above average, even though not at the same level as the S-Tier options. Even so, they are solid choices for your team, especially if they are paired with some strong S-Tier players.

B-tier players are average compared to the other available options. That said, you can use some of them on your team, but they can't be the core of it. Yuzo Morisaki is the worst option when it comes to Goalkeepers, and I thought about creating another tier just for him, but ultimately, that felt a little cruel. Ishida will increase his dribble attribute for a short time every time he receives the ball up to three times. This ability makes him somewhat of a good option if you aim to recycle possession.

So, that's all I have at the moment for our Captain Tsubasa Ace tier list. Future game updates and character releases will for sure have an impact on the meta, and so expect this list to change. Do check back on this page if you want to learn about the latest meta!

#4296. Free-To-Play MOBA Pokémon Unite Is Shutting Down In March

The free-to-play MOBA Pokémon Unite will shut down in March, over five years after its 2021 launch. Although a gradual suspension of services begins today, fans will enjoy one last hurrah thanks to a big in-game event running for the remainder of the game’s lifecycle.

Launched in July 2021 for Switch before migrating to iOS and Android later that year, Pokémon Unite was billed as a friendlier take on the MOBA genre popularized by Dota 2 and League of Legends, thanks to its short matches (10 minutes) and simplified mechanics. Despite its initial popularity, the game is winding down and will go offline for good on March 23, 2027.

An End of Service notice on the game’s website reads,

“We offer our sincerest gratitude to the many Trainers who have played since service started for the Nintendo Switch version on July 21, 2021. We would like to express our thanks to everyone by holding a special event until service ends. The Pokémon Unite Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo competitive tournament (an event for Pokémon Unite only) will also be held as previously announced. We hope you continue to enjoy Pokémon Unite until the final day of service. After service ends, the 'Pokémon Unite Game Content Guidelines for Online Platforms' will no longer be published or maintained, and we will no longer provide support regarding use of Pokémon Unite videos and images.”

As of today, in-game sales of Aeos gems and Unite Club memberships/renewals have been suspended. Existing Unite Club members will continue to use their benefits until the end of the membership period.

On November 12, an update will kick off the aforementioned final special event, where players can obtain items such as all Unite licenses and Holoware that have appeared in the game up to that point. A library feature will also be added, letting players view certain records and in-game content even after the game shuts down on March 23. Those who don’t download the library feature before the shutdown date will not be able to get it afterward.

Qualifiers for the Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo Competitive tournament will take place as planned on December 5. After the game shuts down on March 23, players won't be able to log in to Pokémon Unite or play any battles. Only the library feature will remain accessible.

We enjoyed Pokémon Unite when it launched, with executive video editor Alex Van Aken scoring it an 8 out of 10 in his review, writing, “The game eats away the hours of my day as I reassuringly say to myself, 'Just one more match.' Battles play out with the spectacle that the Pokémon series is known for, and with so many abilities to choose from, no match feels the same as the last. The game’s simple mechanics and recognizable characters make for an approachable MOBA experience, and with a potential catalog of nearly 900 Pokémon to pick from, my hopes are high for the future of Pokémon Unite.”

#4295. Internet Provider Offers Free Upgrades to Rush GTA 6 Downloads

Michael Manning (He/Him) has been enamored with video games since he first played the Sonic Classic Collection as a child. With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of ar

With the always-online nature of modern gaming, the internet is a real focus point for players across the globe, and ISPs have become a leading force in gaming, whether they fully step into the space or not.

With two new squadmates, a Long-War style campaign, and a collection of community-led fixes, MENACE is always looking up.

With the lack of actual physical discs able to house the entirety of a modern AAA game, and the spread of download code purchases, solid internet has become all but a requirement to keep up with gaming, even if you’re playing something completely single-player.

Between day-one patches and massive file sizes, slow internet can totally curb the excitement of snagging a new game, adding hours or even days before you’re free to actually play. By jumping in to assist with this problem, Spectrum is definitely earning some points with the general public, an easy win to course-correct some of the annoyances users complain about with the service.

Whether it's for connecting to online lobbies or downloading massive games, ISPs have become a leading force in gaming, whether they fully step into the space or not.

GTA 6 was recently revealed to stack up at a whopping 212 GBs, a solid size for a game of its hype and magnitude, sure to only bloat as the eventual inclusion of multiplayer and extra content looms. For now, though, players are incredibly eager for more about Grand Theft Auto 6’s story, and following spoiler lockdowns from Rockstar, the only place to learn will be by playing.

With that in mind, the scramble to download the game will put some major pressure on both the Microsoft and PlayStation stores, just hopefully not enough to lead to any kind of store outage. Steam has fallen victim to such overuse during major drops like Hollow Knight: Silksong, and even if players have super-fast Wi-Fi, if the store is down, the store is down.

This is the precarious position of a fully online gaming space: only so much bandwidth to go around, and it just adds another thing to pay for to keep up with gaming. Massive downloads and always-on functionality are the reality of the space now, and despite the misgivings, developers have used them to make major strides.

A larger focus on always-online functionality means developers have gotten extremely creative with it over the years, leading to some of the best mechanics in the games they’re in. Death Stranding is one title that makes fantastic use both narratively and mechanically of being always connected with the world at large, but it's hardly the first to do so.

The Souls series’ message system, allowing you to get advice and tricks from anyone else, and even see how they died, is a major mechanic throughout their titles, one that would make the series feel a little hollow if it up and vanished. Despite the pains of maintaining a connection, these titles are genuinely stronger for having it, despite any misgivings or annoyances.

GTA 6 is destined to have a massive online space once its standalone online mode drops, if the sheer popularity of GTA 5 Online is any indication. For now, though, any boost to connection will simply make getting the game easier, a boon many are sure to snatch up as soon as the offer is fully on the table. Everyone wants in on the PR pie of GTA 6, even if their inclusion feels a little out of left field.

#4294. Zenelss Zone Zero Version 2.6 has you playing as an event planner and social media manager for an idol group

Zenelss Zone Zero's Encore for an Old Dream has a good excuse for introducing some new mechanics to the action game.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered a tonne of information about the game’s big upcoming update, Version 2.6. This latest addition kicks off celebrations in New Eridu, and it’s dubbed Encore for an Old Dream.

Version 2.6 is not far off, either, arriving in ZZZ on February 6 - exactly one week from today. Encore for an Old Dream is something of an in-between story that takes place after the end of Season 2.

The narrative of 2.6 sees the Proxies’ return to Sixth Street for New Eridu's annual Gilded Carrot Day. At the centre of the celebrations is the debut of idol group Angels of Delusion at the 404 Error music venue, but not all is as it seems.

The story follows the Proxies getting invited backstage to support the group, which also includes helping them set up practice schedules, organise events and manage social media activities. There’s a rhythm minigame as part of that, along with new maps and mechanics for Marcel Adventure.

Angels of Delusion is also the group that the two new Agents being introduced in this update belong to. Members of the same group are capable of performing coordinated attacks. The new arrivals are Sunna and Aria.

Sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

Aria is the other new arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

Version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a new game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

Beyond all the celebrations, this update also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a new outfit for Pan Yinhu.

The big event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

#4292. Starsand Island is a life and farming sim that isn't gacha, and it's out next week

Starsand Island officially has an Early Access release date, and it sounds like it won't stay there for years.

Though it may seem like we just had a big life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

The game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Seed Sparkle Lab announced today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

The developer said to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access

Starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese New Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

On top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab says you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

You can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

#4290. Nintendo Is Currently Not Considering More Switch 2 Price Changes

Nintendo president, Shuntaro Furukawa, has confirmed that the company is currently not considering any further price changes for the Switch 2 following an increase earlier this year.

This comes via Reuters after Nintendo released its latest financial data, during which it was reported that sales for the Switch 2 dropped over 37% year-on-year, with operating profit sliding 16%.

Despite some concern amongst investors, Furukawa-san has sought to ease this by confirming that Nintendo is currently in a position to secure sufficient quantities of memory as the supply crisis continues.

Nintendo's forecast for the remainder of the fiscal year remains unchanged, so it's currently expecting to shift over 16 million Switch 2 units; a decline from last year, sure, but still an incredibly impressive figure.

Confirmation that no further price changes are on the horizon will no doubt come as a relief for many. The Switch 2's price rose globally earlier this year as a result of market conditions, which has no doubt contributed to the downward turn in sales.

You could certainly argue, however, that the price hike was relatively tame compared to some of the changes taking place at other companies. The Switch 2's price rose by $50 in the US and a mere £24 in the UK. Any price hike is disappointing, of course, but when you consider how expensive the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S are these days, it could be a lot worse.

#4289. Nioh 3 launches, immediately becomes the most played Nioh ever on Steam

Just a few hours after launch, Nioh 3 is already the biggest release in series history on Steam.

It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

This already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is currently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

There are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

Critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. Once you’re ready to get deeper, be sure to read up on how to play co-op with other players, and how to summon AI Acolytes to help you out.
