#4288. Phantom Blade Zero Review – Wuxia Wonder Abounds

Rooted in Wuxian storytelling and scale, built on an impressively detailed combat system, and wrapped in a bloody Chinese martial underground that’s a genuine joy to play in, Phantom Blade Zero is a feat. It joins an echelon of action pedigree that includes Sekiro, Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and just about any other action game you hold in high regard. It hails from developer S-Game, which has dabbled in mobile and smaller-scale games, and I’m shocked by what it’s pulled off with its triple-A action inauguration. But make no mistake: though Phantom Blade Zero is this team’s first crack at a game like this, it is an incredibly confident, strong debut.

Protagonist Soul is a stoic martial arts master betrayed by the Order he’s sworn his life to; he dies and returns to life with only 66 days to live. That’s enough time to settle his debts, repay his betrayers, and end a villainous conspiracy to seize full power of the Wulin realm. This narrative is Phantom Blade Zero's weakest link, but its premise adds enough mystery and tension to keep this Wuxian journey exciting through to its final, realm-shattering moments. Narrative bombshells drop not just through the game’s general fantasy-realism art direction, but also through anime scenes, opera puppet shows, animated brushstroke sequences, and more, highlighting Chinese culture and its integral place in Phantom Blade Zero.

The game features a staggering number of unique enemy types, and though the final hours get a bit repetitive, it’s admirable how long S-Game maintains such a high level of combat-oriented ecstasy. Soul’s access to weapons drives that exhilaration. Every weapon is wholly unique. Because the combat is combo-based, picking up a new weapon feels like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. Each has its own moveset and abilities, with later-game weapons featuring combo lists that look more at home in a Street Fighter menu. Add in the special, tide-turning weapons known as Phantom Edges, with limited charge-based uses, and there’s no shortage of permutations to delightfully experiment with.

Drawing on Chinese cinema, Phantom Blade Zero's setpiece bosses boast a sense of awe and scale only the genre's best typically offer. With virtually no repeat bosses, save for a few in separate trials, it’s impressive how many powerful figures I flayed, and how many delivered a unique fight. I also appreciate the checkpoints between boss phases, as they remove the frustrating repetition of replaying phase one again and again just to take another stab at the second phase I’m struggling with.

You’d be forgiven for assuming Phantom Blade Zero is a Soulslike, given its challenging bosses, interconnected world, and Phantom Bell checkpoints, this game’s equivalent of bonfires. It definitively isn’t, though. The challenge is much more surmountable; the game isn’t interested in making you die over and over, there are difficulty options, and you can equip accessories to make parries and dodges easier. World progression is materially different, too, as enemies don’t respawn after you kill them. It’s an interesting, perhaps blasphemous, choice for the genre, but it's surprisingly effective, adding a sense of worldbuilding and tangible progression I didn’t know I wanted from my action games. Soul is on a mission to remove evil, and mechanically, I’m doing just that. Enemies don’t respawn incoherently just because I heal and save.

Environmental features weave in and out of each other, and the architectural design and layout of these regions lead to many subsequent “aha” moments. S-Game infuses search-action elements into this exploration through the aforementioned Phantom Edges, some of which double as tools to unlock surprising new areas in both new and previously visited biomes. As a result, backtracking and exploration remain fresh. A lot of it is optional, as are some of Phantom Blade Zero's most rewarding elements, including its demanding “perfect” ending. Sadly, this renders other endings unsatisfying, with clear chunks intentionally missing.

Despite forays into the Uncanny Valley, Phantom Blade Zero is visually striking, and the action is brilliantly animated. It’s all set to genre-breaking music, too, with original metalcore songs, operatic choirs, 808s, and traditional Chinese instrumentation, creating a score as illustrious as the action it enhances.

Phantom Blade Zero is an astounding action achievement, almost unbelievably so for a game that is essentially a studio’s genre debut. It is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, one that recognizes the genre’s strengths and weaknesses and addresses both with fantastical Wuxian style. Though the action genre is always jam-packed with new releases, few are as special as Phantom Blade Zero.

#4287. Dragon Ball Legends best teams and combinations

The best teams in Dragon Ball Legends are interesting, to say the least. Lots of good (Zenkai mostly) cards and lots of reliable combinations to play with. Compared to how the game used to be, where there was a clear-cut team above the rest, nowadays it’s almost the exact opposite.

There are maybe three or four S tier team comps and around five more pretty close to that level. Team X will counter team Y, team Z might counter team X while team Y will counter team Z. In that sense, the current meta is more evenly balanced.

Some of the players will prefer to make their own compositions, but first, they would need to know which characters to pick. We suggest you skip checking the best team compositions and focus on Dragon Ball Legends tier list if that's the case. How to pick the DBZ Legends' best teams? But of course, at the end of the day, we want to rank those teams right? That’s why you are here, for the best teams in Dragon Ball Legends. So how are we going to do that? Well, we’ll take into consideration a couple of things. To start, how ‘flexible’ a team is. Let me give you an example. ‘Team A’ has a plethora of units that players can choose from to use as a core for that comp and still be top tier. Compare that to ‘Team B’ where you absolutely need certain units (maxed out) to be ‘as good’. That’s a reason to put team A higher than team B on our list.

Another reason of course is, how well these comps can perform at the moment. Some are more expensive than others due to them having two or three Zenkai core members that need to be maxed out and so on.

Now, if you are an experienced Dragon Ball Legends player, you already know which team comps are good and you have your own opinion about them. But, for new players and also players who were away from the game for a while, this tier list of best teams in DBL will give you a good idea about the current state of the game.

You don't want to waste your resources trying to put together teams that are not really viable at the moment.

So without any further ado, let's dive right into our Dragon Ball Legends' best teams!

A huge category with many units to choose from as the core of the team. Yellow SP Android #18 is a Z+ tier unit and for a good reason. She’s the main damage dealer of this team and the only core unit. Her kit is borderline broken after she received her Zenkai Awakening. Usually, you want to pair her with the tanky SP Android 16 (Green) or SP Android 21 (Blue) and SP Perfect Cell Revived (Red). But those are not your only options. One of the reasons why we put Android team so high on our list of Dragon Ball Legends' best teams is because of how easy you can build it. SP Android 21 Evil (Purple), SP Android 21 Good (Green), SP Super 17# (Green) are some very reasonable alternative options.

There’s nothing this DBL team is lacking pretty really. On top of that, there are really many comps you can make as the category is quite big with lots of top tier units. SP Majiin Buu (Green) and SP Perfect Form Cell (Revived) are usually the go-to choices. SP Demon King Piccolo (Aged) (Purple) after he gets to transform is just a beast of a unit. SP Piccolo (Yellow), SP Buu Kid (Blue), SP Android 21:Good (Green), SP Android 21 (Blue). Saiyan and Son Family can be a problem when you running Regeneration.

Well, it’s Dragon Ball and we are talking about Saiyans. No surprise there. This category keeps getting updates and it has a really big roster. There are many different fighters to choose from (all Zenkai of course) with the SP Super Saiyan Bardock being the only core member. The only other member that you definitely want to have (on your bench) is EX Raditz (Blue). His health-boosting buffs for this team are just too good to pass on. SP Angry Goku (Blue), SP Super Gogeta (Red), SP Super Saiyan 3 Goku (purple and green) are your other choices. It would be a shame if Saiyans didn't make it to the top teams in DB Legends.

When three of the game's top units are the core of this comp, it’s only natural to put it this high on our list. SP SSJ 2 Youth Gohan (Red), SP SSJ3 Goku (Purple) and SP Angry Goku (Blue) is definitely a formidable trio. The issue is that once you replace one of these units, there’s a notable drop-off. At least when we are talking top-tier teams in DBL. So even though this is another big category with many units, you have limited options. Other viable units would be SP Youth Goku (Yellow), SP Super Kaioken Goku (Green), SP Gohan (Adult). Most important to note, is that this is the best team to counter Android.

Strong comp but little to no diversity as your options here are limited. Obviously, everything on Hybrid Saiyans teams is based around SP SSJ 2 Gohan (Youth) (Red) and SP SSJ2 Trunks (Blue) as the main carries. The other two viable options that you have for this comp would probably be SP Goten Kid (Yellow) or SP Trunks Kid (Green).

Now this is a team with many viable core options. The ‘staple’ of this team is SSJ2 Trunks (Blue) pretty much. You can go with SP Goku Black (Green) and SP SSJ2 Trunks (Blue) as your offensive fighters, along with SP SS God Vegeta (Purple). Another comp would be, SP LL SSJ Gohan (Yellow) along with SP SSJ2 Trunks (Blue) and SP Perfect Form Cell (Revived) Red as your defence. There are many top-tier units that can complement Trunks on this team. You can’t really go wrong here.

SP Android 18 (Yellow) is that strong. This category isn’t as big as others on our list and the issue here is that the comp is pretty much fixed. SP Android 21 Green and Blue are the other two members usually on this DBL team. But outside of that, the options are limited. Evel 21 Android Purple, SP Mai (Green) and EX Kakunsa (Green) taking up the rest of the slots. It’s a very aggressive team comp, focusing on 18’s damage output and oppressive toolkit.

SP Super Gogeta (Red) is still the main unit in this team. SP SS God Vegito (Blue) is still relevant. The problem with this comp is the lack of defence. Adding SP Super 17 (Green) is a solution but on the other hand, his toolkit doesn’t synergize very well with Gogeta and Vegito. This team is somewhat outdated but still relevant in the current DBL teams meta.

SP Vados (Green) is an amazing support overall for this team. The other two members here would be SP Super Saiyan God Super Saiyan Goku (Blue) and SP Super Saiyan God Vegeta (Yellow). Great units overall that make up a very strong lineup. Alternatively, you can probably use SP God of Destruction Beerus (Green), SP Super Saiyan God SS Vegeta (Future) (Purple), SP Champa (Yellow). Of course, ideally, you want to pair the two Zenkais (Goku and Vegeta) with Vax'dos, otherwise, the team drops significantly.

#4286. Every Pokémon Gimmick, Ranked

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Over the years, we have seen many different Pokémon gimmicks pop up. It seems like every generation of Pokémon needs to have its own gimmick to make it stand out from the others.

It has come to a point where many fans of the series are tired of seeing new gimmicks pop up, and they would rather Pokémon go back to its roots with simple turn-based battles.

Unfortunately, that is never going to be the case, so you must accept whatever gimmick is in each game. Some of these gimmicks aren’t bad, but other ones are rather questionable. Let’s compare each of these gimmicks and see how they stack up against each other.

After introducing Mega Evolutions to Pokémon, Game Freak needed something to top it. Unfortunately, the gimmick in the next games, Sun and Moon, ended up being what is considered the worst gimmick in the Pokémon series.

The gimmick in question is Z-Moves. Z-Moves allow your Pokémon to use a massively powerful move, provided they are holding the appropriate Z-Crystal. Many have said that requiring an item to use one all-powerful move is a bit lame.

These all-powerful moves are often viewed as the one-hit option, allowing you to clear battles easily without much strategy being involved. The gimmick often felt unbalanced, and the addition of annoying, unskippable cutscenes, made using the moves extremely annoying.

I am someone who absolutely loves the Paldea region. I think that it is a beautiful area, and the idea that battles are celebrated in massive arenas is actually really cool to me. However, this generation of Pokémon games has one of the worst gimmicks, and that is Dynamaxing.

Dynamaxing allows a Pokémon to grow massive, amplifying its power in the process, and giving it access to different moves. In theory, it sounds decent. However, it is a nightmare for competitive play, as it makes already extremely powerful Pokémon even more powerful instead of lifting up and helping weaker Pokémon.

In addition to this, the moves given to the Pokémon are not unique, as they become different moves based on the previous move’s type, so a flying-type move will always become the same move when Dynamaxed. There are even more issues with it, but it all boils down to the gimmick feeling like not much thought went into it, as it is rather unbalanced and makes battles a bit of a slog.

Our picks for the best Pokémon Champions teams that are sure to help you climb this season.

If you were around for the Ruby and Sapphire days of Pokémon, then you remember double battles. These changed the way that Pokémon battles were played, and then they were expanded on in a rather weird way when triple Battles and rotational Battles appeared in Pokémon Black and White.

These battle types have rarely appeared since their inception, and it is because they weren’t very popular at the time. Triple battles are simple, involving three Pokémon being on the field at once instead of two. This is a bit unnecessary, as double battles were already fine.

Additionally, rotational battles were annoying because you had the ability to rotate your Pokémon around whenever you wanted, making some moves completely obsolete. However, it did make things interesting because the mechanic of rotating your Pokémon was different from switching them in and out of battle.

Terastallization is a gimmick that has the fanbase rather mixed, as there are many who enjoy the mechanic, and then there are those who absolutely hate it. As far as things go, it is a rather middle-of-the-road gimmick that could have been better, but it isn’t that bad.

This gimmick, which was introduced in Pokémon Scarlet and Violet, allows you to crystalize your Pokémon, changing its typing in the process. Many enjoy the mechanic because it lets you change the Pokémon’s typing, making them more resistant to moves they were once weak against.

The argument against Terastallization is that it can be unbalanced in certain battle formats, but it is mostly a balanced mechanic that works well with the series. The other argument is that every Pokémon looks absolutely terrible when it Terastalizes, and to be honest, they aren’t wrong.

Whether they're unlikely or just silly, these are the Ridiculous Pokémon Mega Evolutions We Would Love To See.

As stated earlier in the article, double battles were introduced in Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire, and they have remained to this day. It is one of the few earlier gameplay gimmicks that people sometimes forget started as a gimmick because it was so beloved.

Never before had players thrown two Pokémon into battle at once, and it felt like a natural progression of the battle system, allowing players to have two Pokémon whose types complimented each other.

Plus, this generation introduced new moves that were meant to be used during double battles. This gimmick has not changed since its inception, and it is because it feels natural for the series. There is nothing that needs to be changed about it, which makes it one of the best Game Freak has added to the series.

Why is it that I always forget that Mega Evolution is something that started in Pokémon X and Y? I always think that it was the gimmick from Pokémon Black and White. Tangent aside, Mega Evolution has become the most popular gimmick that Game Freak has added to the games.

It is so popular that people have continuously asked for more and more Pokémon to receive Mega Evolutions because the transformations are not only cool, but they are meaningful.

When Mega Evolution happens, it can sometimes change a Pokémon’s type, it can change the Pokémon’s ability, and it boosts the Pokémon’s stats tremendously. This can change the tide of a battle, but it isn’t so powerful that it is the ultimate trump card. It doesn’t allow you to blow away the opposition, but rather gives you more of a fighting chance and can dramatically help in certain situations. To this day, there are still Mega Evolutions being created, and it has been the focus in some competitive games as well.

I've missed Pokemon's Mega Evolution mechanic, and it's going to be a huge draw for Pokemon Legends: Z-A players.

#4284. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a new world, and a Fortnite collaboration

Honkai: Star Rail's next major update introduces a whole new planet to the RPG, and way more besides.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the big new world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two new 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

If you log in after launch, you’ll get 20 free pulls and a new free outfit for Ruan Mei. If you play while the Yao Guang fortune event is active, you could earn 1,600 Stellar Jades. You can also expect a free 5-Star character selector to arrive at some point after launch, giving you a free choice between popular (but admittedly a bit old for the meta these days) limited-banner characters Jing Yuan, Kafka, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, Jingliu, Sparkle, Acheron, and Aventurine.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

#4283. Cozy Magical Sim Witchbrook Gets A January Release Date

Witchbrook is a game I've been looking forward to for a while, and today's Nintendo Indie World showcase finally confirmed the game's release date: January 28. Any game from Chucklefish, best known for publishing Stardew Valley and developing the Wargroove series, is worthy of my attention, and Witchbrook looks more exciting the more we see of it. See it for yourself in the release date trailer below.

The game mixes cute pixel art with a robust suite of magical gameplay systems. As you go to a witch college to learn spells, you'll also build a life in the town, making friends, working jobs, decorating your home, and more. It was an appealing pitch when it was announced nearly 10 years ago in 2017, and it remains so to this day. After a long stretch of relative silence, last year the game was scheduled to launch sometime in 2026. Obviously, the team has faced some delays since then, but we're just glad it's actually coming out.

Witchbrook's release date was announced during today's Nintendo-specific stream, but it's coming to all major platforms: PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, Switch, and PC.

#4281. Heartopia shows off My Little Pony collaboration, and there's a pre-launch event to hold you over

Heartopia’s My Little Pony collaboration is close, and the pre-launch event has already kicked off.

Heartopia has officially shared initial details about its first-ever collaboration event. The game, which launched a month ago to great success on mobile, as well as Steam on PC, has already been a staple among fans of Animal Crossing and The Sims.

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

The Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

The first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

The ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

The more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

Badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

#4280. T3 Arena tier list - Heroes ranked from best to worst

Do you want to know the best heroes in T3 Arena? Then you are in the right place. Today, we will share our T3 Arena tier list with you. In it, we have ranked each available hero from best to worst. About T3 Arena T3 Arena is a fast-paced 3v3 multiplayer shooter, which is available on both iOS and Android.

In T3 Arena, you take part in 3v3 battles, with each lasting three minutes. There are various game modes, such as team deathmatch, where you have to get 20 kills collectively before the other team to score a win. There is also a free-for-all, where the first person to reach 12 kills wins and many more different modes.

T3 Arena has been developed by XD Entertainment, the makers of Flash Party. It's a fantastic shooter, which I am already in love with. There are over 30 heroes available in T3 Arena to choose from before jumping into the action.

When you start playing, you will initially begin with just one hero, but as you progress, accumulate trophies, and unlock rewards, you will get more. Each hero has different weapons, stats, and active, passive and ultimate abilities. So it becomes pretty tough to decide which heroes are the best. But don't worry. This is where our T3 Arena tier list comes to the rescue. T3 Arena tier list We have categorised our T3 Arena tier list into four tiers - S, A, B, and C. Heroes in the S tier are the best options, and you should try to choose them while avoiding heroes in tier C.

In the future, more heroes will be added and balance changes will be made, improving some heroes and vice versa. But don't worry. We will keep updating this post so that this tier list remains accurate.

Iris, Victor and Labula are undoubtedly the strongest heroes available in T3 Arena. You might be shocked to see Iris at rank one, as she is more of a support hero. But trust us, in the right hands, she is unbeatable. Whether it's Crystal Assault or FFA, Iris performs excellently thanks to her abilities. Her active skills can literally be spammed, which will keep healing her and her allies, making it difficult for enemies to take your team down.

Victor, on the other hand, is a perfect pick for anyone who likes to play aggressively. He has a massive HP pool of 5500 and a shield of 3500 at its default level. If you upgrade it, the stats go crazy. Victor performs really well in close-range battles. He also has the ability to stun the enemies for a couple of seconds.

Cristina is an easy hero with simple abilities and controls. She is a perfect hero for anyone who likes to play passively. If you want to take your time, take cover, and pick your battles, she will suit your playstyle. Her active ability allows you to place sticky bombs around the corners to damage enemies when they walk near them. You can put down up to three sticky bombs in the same place, which means most enemy heroes will directly die if they are unfortunate enough to step within their radius. An easy kill for you.

You can also plant these sticky bombs on one side of the map and then take out enemies on the other side. If an enemy tries to approach from an area where sticky bombs are placed, you will know when it explodes as you get a mark on your screen, giving you some potentially useful information.

Cristina's ultimate ability is also insane; it can instantly kill the entire enemy team if they fall within the range of the mines. However, it takes a couple of seconds before the mine explodes, so the timing is crucial.

Skadi is the hero that you unlock when you start playing T3 Arena. She is a decent hero for a beginner, being easy to use and learn. If you are a casual player and use the auto-fire option, then Skadi is a great hero to pick. Her primary weapon, the Kraken heavy pistol, works excellently with this enabled, and her abilities are also easy to use. When playing Skadi, you can make aggressive calls and then get out of fights using your active ability. On top of that, her ultimate can go through walls.

Gloria is somewhat similar to Skadi. Again, she is a great beginner's hero. However, compared to Skadi, she is much more versatile as she has different weapons for long and short-range targets. If you have played many shooters in the past, such as PUBG Mobile or COD Mobile, you will love Gloria, as the mechanics of this hero are somewhat similar.

It would be best to avoid picking up heroes listed in tier C, unless you are going for something fun. Though these heroes can do just fine in some instances, such as Jabali, who is good at close-range fights, overall, these heroes are weak.

Jabali's active ability allows you to create an energy barrier that blocks incoming damage, but T3 Arena is a fast-paced shooter; within a second, three heroes will be attacking you from different directions. It makes no sense to protect bullets from one side. And also, you can't shoot when the energy barrier is in effect. Its ultimate is excellent for taking down enemies that have low HP, but what if you have heroes like Victor in the opponent team? You will hardly cause a dent to his HP.

With this, we come to the end of our T3 Arena tier list. For more tips and guides, stay tuned with us.

#4279. Nioh 3 is killing it on Steam with over double the series' highest concurrent player count

People seemingly haven't been able to stop playing Nioh 3 since the moment it came out, and everyone helped push the numbers to unprecedented heights for the series.

Nioh 3 has had a massive weekend on Steam, the type of launch you just don’t often see for Koei Tecmo games. Indeed, this has very clearly been a monumentous release for both the publisher, and developer Team Ninja.

It is also, quite visibly, the most popular Nioh release ever on PC, and it was impressive watching more and more players jump into the game over the weekend and push the numbers higher.

Nioh 3 came out swinging, breaking the series’ Steam concurrent player record immediately after lanch, with 42,822. Anyone keeping up with how well the game has been received, and how much it’s been anticipated by series fans and Soulslike players, would’ve told you that it was only the beginning.

Late on Friday, and several times on Saturday, the game continued achieving new records, setting new peak concurrent levels every couple of hours. It happened again on Sunday, when the game finally settled on its current 88,045 peak concurrent (via SteamDB).

That’s an incredibly healthy player base, but more than that, it’s more than double the previous record holder, Nioh 2, which peaked at 41,325 concurrent players in 2021. Steam players appear to be very happy with the game, too, with over 1,560 reviews and an overall Very Positive rating.

If you’re among the millions who jumped into Team Ninja’s latest, our guides offer a great place to start. These Nioh 3 gameplay tips cover a wide range of subjects; essential reading for newcomers and veterans. You should also consider changing these settings before you jump in, as it’s going to maker your life easier.

For more useful information, catch up with our list of best weapons for Samurai and Ninja, and how to easily play the game in co-op.

#4278. Nintendo Indie World Showcase Recap: Everything We Saw

The year is nearing its conclusion, and the last big AAA titles are rolling out one-by-one. But today, it was all about the independent titles on Nintendo's latest Indie World Showcase, highlighting new games from smaller indie teams coming to the Switch and Switch 2.

Here's everything we saw at the October 2026 Nintendo Indie World Showcase.

Today's Indie World Showcase started with a big headliner, as the long-awaited witch-life simulator Witchbrook got a release date. Chucklefish and Robtality's cozy magical world goes live on January 28, 2027.

Fans of 3D platformers should probably keep an eye on Winds of Viridia, which looks like a colorful game with a lot of interesting movement and exploration. Shark Jump's fantastical platformer is arriving next year, but if the wait's too long, a free demo is coming today on the eShop.

From one of the co-creators of Celeste, City of None has a gorgeous pixelated art style and colors that immediately remind me of Game Boy Color classics. It's a 2D platformer where you leap around, fight enemies, and explore the strange city around you. The jumping and fighting look solid, and I really like the mysterious atmosphere and art direction. City of None's set for sometime in 2027.

The sword-surfing adventure from the makers of Abzu and Journey is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on October 29, 2026 - tomorrow! It's a gorgeous adventure that earned a Must-Play badge from us, so it's worth your time if you like the kinds of gorgeous, beautiful adventures Giant Squid (developer of Abzu) is known for.

Take an overhead camera angle, brawler gameplay, and some John Wick sensibilities, and you've got Tenjutsu, a stylish roguelike where you use your martial arts prowess to tear apart crime syndicates. I really enjoy the look and vibe of this one, and it's from one of the designers of Dead Cells, too. Tenjutsu might be one to keep an eye on when it arrives on Switch 2 in 2027.

RPG fans have been eating well, and it looks like the feast could continue next year with Threads of Time. The time-traveling RPG is coming to both Switch and Switch 2 next summer, and it's looking absolutely gorgeous.

Ah, raccoons. Nature's most adorable little scamps. If you and your friends have ever wanted to live out the dream of being a rambunctious band of raccoons wreaking havoc on the town, Dumpster Gang sets out to give you just that fantasy in March 2027.

I've already enjoyed quite a bit of Super Battle Golf on PC, so I'll tell you now: if you enjoy golf games and want some Mario Party annoy-your-friends antics wound around them, Super Battle Golf should be on your radar for its March 25, 2027 launch on Switch 2.

Another port of a PC multiplayer mainstay, the co-op physics-driven horror-looter R.E.P.O. is coming to Switch 2 in 2027. This is one for the crowd that likes to be scared one moment and laughing hysterically the next.

Rounding out the co-op section, Haunted Paws has you and a pal playing as a pair of pups searching for their person in a haunted mansion. The side-scrolling 3D look makes it seem like a less-scary Little Nightmares, and the concept is pretty fun. Look for this one on Switch and Switch 2 in May 2027, or try out the free demo later today.

Enjoy shrines, towns, and strange night-time journeys into the unknown? Follow a fox girl and her frog friend on an adventure through a strange island in Kitsune: The Journey of Adashino on Switch 2 and Switch in spring 2027. I've said it a few times in this recap, but wow, the art here is great.

The second entry in the slime-collecting, home-building sim adventure is coming to Switch 2. Pick up adorable slimes with your vacuum, build a home for them, and explore the Rainbow Island around you in January 2027. Plus, there's an exclusive in-game item for the Switch 2 version.

From the makers of Cozy Grove, this multiplayer game encourages players to build a home above the clouds with friends and explore the world around them. Spirit Crossing looks like a big world to make your own alongside your pals, starting November 16, 2026 on both Switch and Switch 2.

Want something a little sillier? My Arms Are Longer Now is a game about, well, really long arms. With numerous Australian comedians lending their vocal talents to the project, this seems like it could be a quirky, charming, and delightfully funny experience when it arrives on both Switch and Switch 2 on March 11, 2027.

The delightfully Game Boy-styled critter delivery game Petal Runner is aiming for a full launch. I've played a bit of this one at events over the years, and it's charmed me every time. If you like nostalgic adventures with a surprisingly heartfelt core, you should mark down the March 8, 2027 launch, or check out the free demo arriving later today.

The chaotic coin-pushing game Raccoin is coming to Nintendo Switch 2. It's just like those token-shoving games you remember from arcades but with a number of wild and wacky means of pushing even more coins over the edge run-over-run. Raccoin: Chaos Max Edition hits Switch 2 on November 10, 2026, and a free demo is out later today.

Hasbro Games Junior Collection (Outright Games, 6th Nov, $29.99) - Play Monopoly Jr., Clue Jr., and The Game of Life Jr. Customize your avatar, unlock rewards, and enjoy local multiplayer fun for up to 4 players. Get ready for a big, colorful game night full of laughs, surprises, and “just one more turn!” moments! This collection brings 3 classic junior board games to life in one exciting video game made for kids and families.

Hillthorn (Raw Fury, 10th Nov, $14.99) - Only the foolish and the desperate attempt to wander the mazelike trails of Hillthorn. Even those who know their way may still stumble upon dangerous wildlife or a local villager’s piercing gaze. But a child has gone missing, time is in short supply, and you’re the one being tasked with unraveling the mountain’s secrets. Welcome to Hillthorn, a dark investigation game unlike any other, where the mystery unfolds without a single word spoken.

HorrorVale: Deadluxe Edition (Electric Airship, 31st Oct, $17.99) - Your next-door neighbors are zombies, reanimated monsters deliver the mail and ghosts hide out in your bathroom. Don't worry about anybody you kill along the way–-everyone is already dead! Muahahha! Bash monsters, recruit 30+ friends, and solve brain-buster puzzles! Welcome to the Underworld. . .

Hundred Fires: OPEN VECTOR -Episode 1- (David Amado Fernández, 29th Oct, $6.99) - HUNDRED FIRES: OPEN VECTOR — Episode 1 is a third-person action and stealth adventure set in an alternate Cold War. You play as Merche, a guerrilla and expert thief sent on a mission that quickly turns into something much bigger. Armed with a katana, a pistol and automatic weapons, you'll have to infiltrate secret facilities, deal with enemy soldiers and uncover the secrets behind the mysterious Ancient Weapons. The katana is at the heart of the game. Use it in combat, but also use it to cut through parts of the environment.

Kingdom of Night (DANGEN Entertainment, 5th Nov, $17.99) - Kingdom of Night is an 80s-inspired isometric action RPG where coming-of-age drama meets cosmic horror. When a satanic cult unleashes the ancient evil Baphomet on the small town of Miami, Arizona, high school student John must fight through a night of demonic chaos to rescue his friends before the town is lost forever. Choose from five distinct classes—Barbarian, Knight, Rogue, Necromancer, or Sorcerer—and customize your build with expansive skill trees, powerful loot, and unique equipment.

K-Pop Rising – Dream to Shine (Microids, 5th Nov, $34.99) - Make your dream come true and become a K-Pop Star in this exciting life sim and rhythm game! Together with your best friend Nova, you've always dreamed of making your mark in the world of K-Pop… Now it's time to shine! Throw yourself into the race for fame and let your talent sparkle, from the practice rooms to the stage! Create a group that reflects who you are and, together, set out to conquer the world's biggest stages. Take inspiration from your idols and grow your fan community on social media! Music is your world, and passion is your driving force: you are the future of K-Pop!

LightQb (Restless Corp, 5th Nov, $9.99) - Twenty-three handcrafted levels. One directional dash. And a narrator who will not let a single mistake go unmentioned. LightQb is a fast, unforgiving first-person platformer built entirely around movement. Chain dashes, air control and raw momentum to fly through neon structures, then do it all again a second faster.

Lilac ~side Witch~ (Frontwing, 5th Nov, $24.99) - A fantasy visual novel set in a magic school where humans and mages mingle. Follow Emil, a young human who despises mages, and Henri, a self-proclaimed "bonehead" of a mage, as they learn how to connect in spite of various anxieties and differing backgrounds. Features numerous beautiful characters designed by industry veteran Oyari Ashito! Lilac Academy.

Lilac ~side Wizard~ (Frontwing, 5th Nov, $24.99) - A fantasy visual novel set in a magic school where humans and mages mingle. Follow Emil, a young human who despises mages, and Henri, a self-proclaimed "bonehead" of a mage, as they learn how to connect in spite of various anxieties and differing backgrounds. Features numerous beautiful characters designed by industry veteran Oyari Ashito! Lilac Academy.

Make it! Karaage (SAT-BOX, 5th Nov, $6.99) - Let's make karaage on Nintendo Switch! Marinate the meat in sauce, coat it in batter, and fry it until crispy! Pack up the finished karaage and add toppings to match each order! Share Joy-Con, and up to 4 players can play together! Reach for the ultimate high score! Make karaage to order! Keep cooking until time runs out!

Next of Kin: Epiphany (Spelkvall, 5th Nov, $9.99) - Step into the world of "Next of Kin: Epiphany," where you become private detective Dennis Monroe, a relentless investigator driven to catch the infamous "Epiphany Killer," a shadowy figure who has haunted the city for over twenty years. Every clue draws you closer to the truth, but danger lurks behind every revelation. In the thrilling conclusion to the "Next of Kin" trilogy, you'll explore atmospheric locations, interrogate suspects with the powerful new "Expose" system, and unravel the chilling truth behind the notorious "Epiphany Killer".

Nyghtmare: The Ninth King (Caracal Games, 31st Oct, $4.99) - Centuries after vanishing without a trace, the Kingdom of Mortemire suddenly reappears. Alongside it awakens Aryn, a young woman strangely unaffected by the mysterious call surrounding the kingdom. Armed with only an iron whip, she ventures into its decaying streets in search of answers, facing the creatures and dangers that have taken hold of the land. Nyghtmare: The Ninth King is a dark-fantasy retro "Vania" experience.

Prinny Party: Going Overboard! (NIS America, 11th Nov, $29.99) - Get your friends together for Prinny Party: Going Overboard! Shelterra the Skyworld (KEMCO, 5th Nov, $17.99) - Soar into an epic fantasy RPG adventure across Shelterra, a vast floating continent untouched by the mysterious corruption known as Odium. Shrek 2 Remastered (Aspyr, 10th Nov, $26.99) - Journey through the fairytale kingdom of Far Far Away from Shrek’s swamp to Fiona’s castle and everywhere in between, in a classic action-adventure experience inspired by the DreamWorks Animation movie. The Slormancer (Plug In Digital, 5th Nov, $24.99) - The Slormancer is an epic 2D Action-RPG Dungeon Crawling game following a band of outcasts on their fight against hordes of enemies led by The Slormancer! Play as a Mighty Knight, a Fierce Huntress or a Mischievous Mage, master hundreds of abilities and ancestral powers, gear up, fight for the reputation of your kind and prove your value to the realm. Put your thinking power to the test in humorous iterations of the problem. Unlock a variety of minigames where you can put your gaming skills to the test. Challenge yourself and learn important and useful philosophical knowledge while expanding your mind! #4275. Best planes in Wings of Heroes

It's time to think like a WW2 pilot to dominate the skies - which is where our handy guide to the best planes in Wings of Heroes swoops in to save the day!

Updated on November  7th, 2026 - Version 2.3.3 - Added: Lockheed P-38G Lightning, Messerschmitt Bf 110 G-2, North American A-36 Apache, Reggiane Re.2001 CN, Supermarine Spitfire Mk IIa

Wings of Heroes is a multiplayer game inspired by the Second World War, and since there are lots of planes, you probably won't have the resources to maintain them all. And while it's always tempting to pick a plane based on its looks alone (we've all judged a book by its proverbial cover, haven't we?), it's worth strategising the best stats for each plane to dominate the skies across every tier.

If you're feeling overwhelmed, fret not - I've shared the best planes in Wings of Heroes in each tier.

Of course, I suggest you take it with a grain of salt, because there is no "one plane fits all" answer here. From fighters to bombers, each one comes with different stats, so choosing something that fits your preferred play style will make a difference.

And speaking of WW2, you might fancy grabbing freebies for some interesting war-themed romps on mobile too! Why not have a go at these Last War Survival codes and Era of Warfare gift codes? Types of aircraft in Wings of Heroes:

Both of these are equal in terms of power. They are not ideal, since they are LF aircraft, but at least you get to learn how to manoeuvre the other planes once you have access to them.

For a Tier II plane, this Fighter is incredibly fast and has a relatively short turn time. It deals good DPS, but it has very (VERY) low survivability. I recommend you use it for the agility it has, but pay attention to the enemy shots, because things can get heated pretty fast.

Although this bomber is a slow one, it is a great choice if you want a well-rounded aircraft. It deals good damage, it has good survivability, and it manoeuvres as well as any other Tier III plane. I particularly like the damage potential it has.

This fun little aircraft is swift and deadly. It has fairly low survival rates, but it has speed, and it can turn in as little as 18 seconds. It also deals okay-ish damage, but you need to be careful with the hits. If you get hit a little bit too much, things could get dangerous.

These three aircraft from Tier V are just amazing. If you manage to upgrade them to max rank, they can be bonkers well into the late game. While the Junkers can deal amazing DPS, it has slightly lower turn time, but crazy survivability. You can sit there and tank, while you eliminate pretty much anybody standing in your way.

As for the other two MFs, they have balanced stats, but a really large arsenal. They also have suspended armaments, which can come in handy. They are both balanced, but deadly. I particularly like the PE-2-31.

These two bombers are pretty similar. They are not too slow to deem them unusable, and they are packed full of missiles and weaponry that deal well over 120 DPS. If you like bombers, one of these two is a must-have. I would personally lean more towards the Mitsubishi one.

The BF 110 G-2 is a reliable multirole fighter. It can deal good damage, it can go fast (so you can catch up with the opponents), and it has okay armour. It's got a relatively decent turn time, and the DPS is something else. The best part is, if you manage to land your suspended armament (the missile), you can one-shot pretty much any opponent.

This outstanding Japanese bomber is fitted with enough firepower to take on an entire enemy squad. It has really good armour, the speed is decent, and although the turn time is higher than you would like, it doesn't deem it unusable. The suspended 8 armaments it has deal okay DPS, and when combined with the 5 other weapons, it's a kill machine.

The Spitfire Fighter is one of the fastest ones you can get your hands on. It deals good damage and is the complete opposite of the Flying Fortress. As the name suggests, the latter is an absolute unit, fitted with heavy weaponry and a turn time that rivals that of the Titanic sinking.

The Flying Fortress is SLOW, but it packs a big, flaming punch. As for the Spitfire, it is super fast, and it is all-around a good choice if you want to hound an enemy.

The P-51 Mustang is an outstanding plane that can deal lots of damage no matter the situation. If you manage to unlock it, it's a must-play.

#4274. Metria tier list: Ranking all currently available characters

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version: 6.3.0 - Added: [Green Hammer Knight] Popodero, [Purple Piercer Knight] Zescole

Asobimo’s Metria has captured our interest recently, and despite a relatively small roster for a game of its type, each of the playable characters featured has its own appeal. But for those more concerned about stats than other attributes, what’s important is knowing where they place and what you should be going for.

While set up like a traditional JRPG, Metria more closely resembles a hack 'n slash. Rather than using a given set of characters in a turn-based setup, you'll be constantly switching between them during quickly moving, flowing battles against a variety of enemies. Spacing and dodging will be your friend, but being able to do damage and make use of your moves is also key to success.

Given that the roster is fairly limited currently, there aren't any downright "bad" characters - we're going to keep the rankings to the S-B tiers. We'll be sure to revisit when more characters are released, especially if Metria manages to find its footing and start making an even bigger splash.

You'll also want to use our reroll guide to Metria as well, but for a brief overview, you should know that each character has an element with which they're in affinity. This boosts their damage against enemies weak to that type and means that they will also take greater damage in certain situations. Characters also have four slots where you can apply upgrades in the form of tarot cards, some of which provide extra boosts to certain characters or those with a certain affinity.

If you take a look at whatever characters you get, you can open the details tab to see all their damage types, stats and more broken down. We also have a guide taking you through the beginning of the game and explaining all the basic mechanics if you want to know more!

That’s where our latest Metria tier list comes in - we’ll be looking at the currently available characters, ranking them based on our experience and their usefulness, and discussing why we’ve made these placements! So let’s get started with…

The top of the Metria tier list is where the best characters, stats and intuitiveness-wise, are placed, starting with the demi-human Aru. One of the indisputably good characters stat-wise, Aru also uses ranged attacks, which makes her one of the few characters to do so. She’s also available from early on and her abilities in this case make a big difference in pushing her into the top tier.

Stats-wise, Rio is nothing to write home about. However, if you’ve ever played a Japanese hack ‘n slash or JRPG, you’ll recognise him as your bog-standard protagonist. Conversely, this means he’s also easy to learn and has a very intuitive move set, so keeping him as the standard centre of your party is an easy recommendation to make.

This tier is where we're placing characters that are easy to learn but perhaps not the ultimate stats-wise. Starting with Lunaria, Begius’ daughter and currently the only magic user in the game, technically speaking. Lunaria’s abilities mix up what has up until now in the game's roster been a fairly consistent style of play between ranged and melee.

Possessing similar debuff abilities to Shash, Zescol is a melee character that offers good stats and the ability to capitalise on debuffs. Since most enemies close the gap quite quickly, she’s a good pick if you want to bring their stats down but not try to keep at a distance as you would with Shash.

It’s often said that Japanese developers are surprised by the popularity of cool old guy characters in their games. Asobimo seems aware of this, as Begius is one of the characters you’ll have from almost near the beginning, and his defensive playstyle makes him good for durability and big hits.

While not bad by any means, characters in B tier are just lacklustre to use at the moment, or simply have better versions in other characters. Dino’s focus on the earth element, for example, isn’t exactly a stand-out given that you’ll likely have access to Begius beforehand, and his move set does it better. However, as you may have noticed, there aren’t really any terrible characters at the moment, but you’ve still got better options.

While Lucas does usually hit a bit higher in some players’ estimations, we found that his move set simply doesn’t measure up to what other characters have available. He’s not a bad pick, stats-wise, of course, but Rio is easier to learn, and other characters have better abilities. He’s nonetheless a solid third pick for your team.

You’ll notice that the character roster essentially doubles when you take into account the SSR versions of characters. Unlike other games, these aren’t just palette swaps, but they entirely switch up a character’s playstyle, including their element. Solid Aqua Shield Begius, for example, switches his element from earth to water, and offers a surprising way to refresh his playstyle.

You can roll these in the gacha, and if you need to know more about currency uses, you can check out our guide to Metria's currency. You'll note that win rates are, naturally, quite low. Fortunately, Metria is one of many gachas now offering pity pulls, offering a guaranteed SSR character after a certain number, which is surprisingly good value with the currently limited roster.

Keep an eye on these, because if you pick one, it may boost - or lower - a character in your estimations. It also offers a reason to play with the gacha system to grab these unique versions of the characters. And since you're a fan of character rankings, you can use our tier list for Battle Cats, and thisInfinite Magicraid tier list. If there are other gachas that you enjoy, take a look around! The chances are we've covered it.

#4273. Love and Deepspace ushers in the Year of the Horse with a Wuxia-inspired AU multi-banner and a restaurant management mini-game

A new Love and Deepspace banner event is here with a lot of rewards to earn, and brand-new Memories for all five lads to unlock.

Love and Deepspace has kicked off the next big in-game moment and is celebrating Chinese New Year with the arrival of a new 5-Star Memory Series. This year's spring-themed banner is available now until February 27, and it comes with a host of events.

The Mortality’s Tenderness banner features five new limited-time 5-Star Memories, one each for the game’s five love interests. The theme is all about warmth, reunion, and intimacy, taking place in a Wuxia-inspired setting that's once again an alternate universe from the main story of the game.

The new memory cards are Xavier: Blades with Blossoms, Zayne: Entwined Kites, Rafayel: Carved Gemheart, Sylus: Shared Lanterns, and Caleb: Clearday Return. You can pick three of the five to focus on and further pick one to guarantee on your second 5-star pull; and you can earn wish rewards by making cumulative wishes over the course of the event.

Some of the rewards you could get include limited headwear, Limited Deepspace Wishes, and — of course — Memory-themed outfits and hairstyles inspired by the new Memories. Outside of wish rewards, the Memory Series comes with growth tasks that rewards you with in-game materials for levelling up the new cards during the event. When you reach Rank 1 for any new Memory from the banner, you’ll earn a Memory-themed outfit with a special colour that matches your chosen love interest.

Illusio returns as part of the new event, too, letting you customise the look of Kindled Moments across all five new Memories. Things you can customise include selecting the outfits and accessories for each love interest, so you can recreate Kindled Moments in your own style. As always, Kindled Moments will go back to their default look after the event ends.

There’s a new mini-game to play, too, available only during the event. It’s called Courteous Fare, a frantic but familiar restaurant management simulation that allows you to unlock a variety of rewards.

Furthermore, if you log in for 10 days throughout the event, you can unlock a new outfit set, Wealth Overflow, which can be worn by any of the love interests as well as the heroine. There are other login rewards, too, like 10 Deepspace Wishes, 10 Empyrean Wishes, His and My Outfit sets, two dynamic portrait photo poses, and loads more.

Finally, the Golden Fortune event adds even more daily log in rewards in the form of one free "shake" per day, from which you can earn a random reward of between 68 and 108 Diamonds — that adds up to a total of 1,296 Diamonds if you show up every day.

#4270. 10 Legendary Grenades and Ordnances You Should Have in Borderlands 4

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

There are various types of legendary items in Borderlands 4, and it goes without saying that they are some of the best items in the game. Because of this, you will want to fill your endgame build with legendary items galore.

The main items you will be using across your builds are weapons, shields, and grenades. Once you have some powerful legendary weapons and have acquired a shield, you will need to focus on getting either a strong grenade or a strong ordnance. For a primary weapon, consider the best legendary assault rifles.

There are numerous legendary grenades and ordnances in Borderlands 4, and several of them are must-have items at this point in the game to refine your build with.

There are some grenades that you have to be careful about where you throw them, and then there are grenades that many refer to as “throw and forget” grenades. This is because you don’t need to worry about where you throw them. Instead, you can toss it in a general direction and go.

The Swarm is a grenade you can forget about because it homes in on targets. Its ability, Swoosh, makes it spawn three homing grenades on impact, and those spawn additional homing grenades for a total of nine.

If you happen to get bonuses on this build that increase your grenade damage and explosion size, you will be living the dream. You can get the Swarm from Sidney Pointylegs in Hungering Plain.

If you are someone who wants to use ordnances, your options are somewhat limited, as there aren’t as many of them in the game, but they are quite powerful. One of the more powerful ones is the Disc Jockey.

This heavy launcher has the ability Bouncing Biscuits, which makes it so it launches energy discs that bounce off surfaces. Each time one of these discs bounces, the damage of the disc increases by 20%.

This is a weapon that is great in small rooms, as the bounces can rack up some serious damage on groups of enemies. You can get this weapon from Sidney Pointylegs in Hungering Plain.

It is interesting whenever a grenade doesn’t deal grenade damage and instead gets all its power from another source. In the case of the Barb’ara, it gets its damage from your skill damage buffs, making it perfect for those who are running skill builds.

This grenade has the ability Tentacles, which causes it to create a tentacle explosion on impact. The explosion created by this impact deals skill damage. These tentacles will spawn two additional grenades that create more tentacles, also dealing skill damage.

Since every Vault Hunter in the game can run a skill build, this is a great grenade to have whenever you decide to switch up your build. You can farm this grenade from Crazed Earl in the Vault of the Damned DLC.

There are plenty of weapons in Borderlands 4 that have been added in DLC. Which ones of them are the best?

Sometimes you just want to fire a rocket launcher and let it delete your problems. In this case, the problem is usually a group of enemies or a massive boss that is blocking your path. The Loiter Sploiter is designed to take care of these problems quickly, and is great if you have an ordnance-focused build and amp gear.

The Loiter Sploiter’s ability, Sploiter, makes it so this weapon fires high-damage rockets. These rockets then spawn additional rockets when they explode, causing massive amounts of damage.

If you are running gear with the amped ability, this will power up these rockets, making them capable of one-shotting bosses with ease. You can get this weapon Infamous Dave in the Murders & Acquisitions DLC.

There are some grenades in Borderlands 4 that don’t just explode. Instead, they have some quirky effects such as shooting lasers or a machine gun at enemies before they explode. Either way, you get an explosion.

The Alignment is one of those grenades, as it has the ability Coordinated, which makes it so the grenade seeks out an enemy when thrown, hovers above them, shoots them with a beam of elemental energy, and then divebombs them.

It is an interesting effect that makes that weapon great for dealing elemental status effects, and therefore, is good for those who want an elemental status effect build. You can obtain this grenade from the Warped & Weird Vault Card.

Speaking of the weird and quirky, the Heimdahl is perhaps the weirdest of the ordnance weapons in Borderlands 4. This is because the weapon shoots Dahl soldier heads that attack enemies. They are out for revenge, and will kill anyone in their way.

The ability of this weapon is called Rig. It fires soldier heads that fly around the battlefield, track down enemies, and vomit on them. This deals significant damage, and is a weapon that you can fire and forget since it tracks enemies.

This weapon is perfect for Vault Hunter builds where you don’t need to worry about ordnance ammo, as you can just keep firing it and clear out a room in no time. You can obtain this weapon from Captain Willis in The Maelstrom in the Vault of the Damned DLC.

There are plenty of legendary assault rifles in Borderlands 4, and we will show you how to get them all.

The Blockbuster grenade is one that will clear an area with ease, but you better make sure to stay out of the area or you will get killed. This grenade is designed to do one thing, which is to cause numerous explosions.

The ability of this grenade is called Got You Covered, and it does give you plenty of cover. This ability makes the grenade split into four grenades on impact. These grenades then spawn an additional two grenades. This sounds normal until you realize that these grenades all bounce in place, creating explosions as they do.

It will cover the field in explosions, and you just need to stay out of the way so you don’t get killed. You can get this grenade from Vile Lictor in Terminus Range.

The Firepot is similar to the Swarm grenade, but it focuses on dealing fire damage and it loves to stick grenades to enemies. Torgue returns with one of the finest grenades in Borderlands 4, and it packs a serious punch.

The ability of this grenade is called Spicy, and it makes the grenade spawn homing Torgue sticky grenades that attach to enemies. In total, nine grenades will spawn from this bad boy, and they will each explode after 13 seconds, igniting the enemies that are unfortunate enough to be hit by them.

It is another throw and forget style grenade that does an amazing job covering the field without you needing to focus too much on what you are doing. You can get this grenade from Leader Willem in Grindstone of the Worthy.

The Waterfall was one of my first legendary grenades in Borderlands 4, so it holds a special place in my heart, and it might be a bit weaker than some of the other weapons on this list. However, this doesn’t mean that it isn’t worth getting, as it packs a serious punch.

This grenade has the Waterfall ability, which makes it explode multiple times whenever it hits an enemy. Throw it in a group, and each enemy damaged by the grenade will cause another explosion, cascading the damage over the surrounding area.

It can wipe out groups of enemies easily, but it is noticeably not as effective as the Swarm. You can get this grenade by farming Bio-Bulkhead in the Dissected Plateau.

There are some grenades and ordnances that can clear out entire rooms, and then there are some that are focused on one thing, and that is killing bosses. The Draupner is basically a delete button for life’s problems, and it is amazing.

Return Wave is the name of the Draupner’s ability, and it makes the weapon fire out three saw blades in a horizontal pattern from the weapon. These saw blades return to you after two seconds or upon impact, effectively hitting enemies twice over.

This ordnance effectively diminishes the damage numbers of every other ordnance in the game, making it a must-have weapon. You can obtain it by running the Takedown at the Hadron Abyss.

There are plenty of legendary weapons in Borderlands 4, but these are the weapons that you should have at this point if you want a strong build.

#4269. Super Auto Pets tier list for November 2026

Are you looking for a Super Auto Pets tier list? Well, you're in luck, since we just made one especially for you. In it, we've ranked the pets from the best to the worst.

For those of you who don't know, Super Auto Pets is a multiplayer strategy (auto chess) game that was released on the 24th of September 2021 by Team Wood Games. This free-to-play game is available on iOS, Android, Steam, and even browsers. The synopsis is simple as can be - you pick a pet with which to fight shoulder-to-shoulder against other players.

SUPER AUTO PETS TIER LIST It's time to talk about pets in detail! At the time of writing this article, there are 166 pets available, which are divided into different sub-categories. Some can be obtained through the shop, and some in exclusive packs. Each pet has a special ability that works well when paired with others. For such mechanics to work to your advantage, a good strategy is needed, as well as an understanding of which character will be profitable and powerful. That is why this Super Auto Pets tier list of the best pets was created - it will make everything less complicated for you!

Pets that are at the top of our Super Auto Pets tier list are the ones that you should build your team around. They are the meta-characters right now, and you need to level them up as fast as possible because of the value they bring to your squad.

You definitely won't go wrong by using the A-tier characters because they are all quite good, but you also have to take into account their abilities. They may require a small amount of additional investment to be as effective as the options in the higher tier.

The majority of pets that fall within the B-tier are quite average. They are not outstanding, but they can come in handy when facing certain foes and in certain teams. While they're still acceptable, there's a limit to how much you can rely on them.

C-tier pets aren't worth investing in, but if there are no other options, these pets will also do - at least, initially. Some of them that have synergies with others can turn out quite useful (like Camel), but only if they are a part of a certain team.

When it comes to pets on this tier, it is worth mentioning that they lose out on many points to the pets on the tier list above, but they are still playable.

It's better not to consider these pets for investment during a battle, as they bring very few buffs and will do nothing but take up a slot in the team. Some of them, like Beetle, can be useful in the first round, but other than that, just avoid them. They are at the bottom of the Super Auto Pets tier list for a reason.

Our Super Auto Pets tier list was created to make the game easier to tackle, but it's in no way intended to discourage you from playing whatever you prefer. If you have personal preferences, then feel free to go with those. Just remember, the game will likely pose a greater challenge than it needs to! But maybe that's how you prefer it! We hope this guide was helpful for you - and while you are here, take a look at our list of the best strategy games for Android.

#4268. Battlefield 6's next season will speed up battle pass progression, and make it so Redsec players who don't own the game can actually make progress

Season 2 of Battlefield 6 looks to bring a host of broad, positive changes to XP, progression, audio and more.

Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the new content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

We know that Season 2 is introducing a big new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

The real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the new season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

Movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

#4267. "You Don't Want To Interrupt The Player's Experience" - Here's Why Zelda's Switch 2 Remake Cut Some Mario References

Nintendo is known in recent times for dropping Star Fox (and even Pikmin) into the Super Mario universe, but with the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on the Switch 2, it decided to take a little more care.

In the castle courtyard, where Link meets with Zelda, you might have noticed how the character portraits for Mario and friends are not in the Switch 2 version of the game. If you are wondering about the thought process behind this, Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma has explained how the team didn't want to break the immersion.

Here's what he had to say during the same chat with Game Informer:

Eiji Aonuma: "Certainly, at the time, when we put those [portraits] there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal. Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing. But looking at it now, like if a player is coming through that area, and given the overall way that we're, you know, creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, "Why is Yoshi there?” We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time."

If you recall, the 3DS game also had Skyward Sword art hidden in certain locations, and this is also gone from the Switch 2 remake. According to Aonuma, the same reasoning applies here - the team didn't want to "interrupt the player's experience by seeing something that's unrelated to what they're currently doing in the game".

Although these easter eggs are gone, certain references to the Mario series remain intact as they are part of the character designs:

"You will remember that there is one design element on Talon with Bowser on it, and that's part of the original design of the character. So we didn't change that. That stays as is."
